plainContent: On this page you will find a climate change paragraph in 150, 250 and 300 words for Class 6 to 12, SSC and HSC. The short version suits junior classes, while the longer versions suit SSC and HSC. A Bangla meaning, important word meanings and exam tips are given at the end. Climate Change Paragraph in 150 Words Best for Class 6–7. Climate change means a long-term change in the earth's weather patterns. The earth is slowly becoming warmer because heat-trapping gases are entering the atmosphere. Vehicles, factories and power stations release these gases, and cutting down forests makes the problem worse. A warmer planet brings irregular rain, longer heat waves, stronger storms and rising sea levels. These changes are serious for Bangladesh. Floods and cyclones can damage homes and crops, while salt water may enter fields and drinking-water sources. Poor families suffer most because they have fewer resources to rebuild their lives. Farmers lose crops, and many people lose their homes and livelihoods. We cannot solve this problem with one action. The government should protect forests, develop clean energy, improve warning systems and plan climate-resilient towns. We can save electricity, plant and protect trees, reduce waste, and use buses or bicycles when possible. Education is important because informed people make better choices. Careful decisions today can protect future generations. Climate Change Paragraph in 250 Words Best for Class 8–10 and SSC. Climate change means a long-term change in the earth's weather patterns. The earth is slowly becoming warmer because heat-trapping gases are entering the atmosphere. Vehicles, factories and power stations release these gases, and cutting down forests makes the problem worse. A warmer planet brings irregular rain, longer heat waves, stronger storms and rising sea levels. Melting ice in cold regions also adds water to the oceans. These changes are serious for Bangladesh, a low-lying country with many rivers and a long coastline. Floods and cyclones can damage homes, roads and crops, while salt water may enter fields and drinking-water sources. Poor families suffer most because they have fewer resources to rebuild their lives. Farmers lose crops, fishermen lose their catch, and many people lose their homes and livelihoods. When people lose their income, children may even have to leave school. We cannot solve this problem with one action. The government should protect forests, develop clean energy, improve warning systems and plan climate-resilient towns. It should also build strong embankments and shelters in coastal areas. Citizens can save electricity, plant and protect trees, reduce waste, and use buses or bicycles when possible. Education is important because informed people make better choices. Careful decisions today can protect future generations. Climate change is not a distant issue. It is already affecting our weather, our food and our homes. If we act together — government, citizens and students — we can reduce future damage and protect the lives and livelihoods of coming generations. Climate Change Paragraph in 300 Words Best for SSC and HSC. Climate change means a long-term change in the earth's weather patterns. The earth is slowly becoming warmer because heat-trapping gases are entering the atmosphere. Vehicles, factories and power stations release these gases, and cutting down forests makes the problem worse. A warmer planet brings irregular rain, longer heat waves, stronger storms and rising sea levels. Melting ice in cold regions also adds water to the oceans. Scientists warn that if this warming continues, the effects will become more severe. These changes are serious for Bangladesh, a low-lying country with many rivers and a long coastline. Floods and cyclones can damage homes, roads and crops, while salt water may enter fields and drinking-water sources. Poor families suffer most because they have fewer resources to rebuild their lives. Farmers lose crops, fishermen lose their catch, and many people lose their homes and livelihoods. When people lose their income, children may even have to leave school. The burden of climate change therefore falls hardest on those who contributed least to causing it. We cannot solve this problem with one action. The government should protect forests, develop clean energy, improve warning systems and plan climate-resilient towns. It should also build strong embankments and shelters in coastal areas. Citizens can save electricity, plant and protect trees, reduce waste, and use buses or bicycles when possible. Students can also spread awareness in their families and communities. Education is important because informed people make better choices. Careful decisions today can protect future generations. Climate change is not a distant issue. It is already affecting our weather, our food and our homes. If we act together — government, citizens and students — we can reduce future damage and protect the lives and livelihoods of coming generations. The earth is our only home, and saving it is the duty of every one of us. excerpt: On this page you will find a price hike paragraph in 150, 250 and 300 words for Class 6 to 12, SSC and HSC. The short version suits junior classes, while the
plainContent: On this page you will find a price hike paragraph in 150, 250 and 300 words for Class 6 to 12, SSC and HSC. The short version suits junior classes, while the longer versions suit SSC and HSC. A Bangla meaning, important word meanings and exam tips are given at the end. Price Hike Paragraph in 150 Words Best for Class 6–7. Price hike means a sustained rise in the prices of everyday goods and services. When rice, vegetables, fuel, medicine, rent or transport becomes more expensive, families must spend more money for the same standard of living. The burden is heaviest for poor people and workers whose incomes do not rise with the market. Prices may rise because of inflation, higher fuel and production costs, floods or other disasters, shortages, transport problems, hoarding and excessive profit-taking. A disruption in one part of the supply chain can raise the final price in the shop. The result can be anxiety, less nutritious food, postponed treatment and greater poverty. The government can respond by ensuring adequate supply, improving storage and transport, monitoring markets, taking action against illegal hoarding, and helping families in genuine difficulty. Consumers should compare prices, avoid waste, and not create artificial shortages by panic buying. A coordinated effort can protect both producers and buyers while the economy stabilises. Price Hike Paragraph in 250 Words Best for Class 8–10 and SSC. Price hike means a sustained rise in the prices of everyday goods and services. When rice, vegetables, fuel, medicine, rent or transport becomes more expensive, families must spend more money for the same standard of living. The burden is heaviest for poor people and workers whose incomes do not rise with the market. Even a small rise in the price of rice or cooking oil can upset the monthly budget of a poor family. Prices may rise because of inflation, higher fuel and production costs, floods or other disasters, shortages, transport problems, hoarding and excessive profit-taking. A disruption in one part of the supply chain can raise the final price in the shop. For example, when floods damage crops, the supply of vegetables falls and prices climb. When fuel becomes dearer, the cost of carrying goods also rises. The result of a price hike is painful for ordinary people. Families cut down on nutritious food, delay medical treatment, and reduce spending on education. Children may suffer from poor nutrition, and the elderly may skip their medicines. Anxiety grows in every household, and poverty increases. The gap between the rich and the poor becomes wider. The government can respond by ensuring adequate supply, improving storage and transport, monitoring markets, taking action against illegal hoarding, and helping families in genuine difficulty. Consumers should compare prices, avoid waste, and not create artificial shortages by panic buying. A coordinated effort can protect both producers and buyers while the economy stabilises. When rice, vegetables, fuel, medicine, rent or transport becomes more expensive, families must spend more money for the same standard of living. The burden is heaviest for poor people and workers whose incomes do not rise with the market. Even a small rise in the price of rice or cooking oil can upset the monthly budget of a poor family. A family that once lived comfortably on its income may suddenly find it hard to buy the same amount of food. Prices may rise because of inflation, higher fuel and production costs, floods or other disasters, shortages, transport problems, hoarding and excessive profit-taking. Families cut down on nutritious food, delay medical treatment, and reduce spending on education. Children may suffer from poor nutrition, and the elderly may skip their medicines. The government can respond by ensuring adequate supply, improving storage and transport, monitoring markets, taking action against illegal hoarding, and helping families in genuine difficulty. International Mother Language Day Paragraph in 150 Words Best for Class 6–7. International Mother Language Day is observed on 21 February to honour the languages spoken by people around the world. The day also recalls the language movement in Bangladesh, when students and citizens protested in 1952 for the right to use Bangla. Several demonstrators lost their lives, and their sacrifice became a lasting symbol of linguistic rights. People mark the day by visiting Shaheed Minar, placing flowers, arranging discussions, holding cultural programmes, and reading poetry. The observance reminds us that language carries history, identity, and knowledge. We should respect our mother tongue, develop it through reading and writing, and show equal respect for other languages. Protecting linguistic diversity helps communities live with dignity and understanding. On 17 November 1999, UNESCO proclaimed 21 February as International Mother Language Day, and it has been observed around the world since 2000. This honour came because of the sacrifice of 1952. International Mother Language Day Paragraph in 250 Words Best for Class 8–10 and SSC. International Mother Language Day is observed on 21 February to honour the languages spoken by people around the world. The day also recalls the language movement in Bangladesh, when students and citizens protested in 1952 for the right to use Bangla as a state language. On 21 February 1952, police opened fire on a peaceful student procession in Dhaka. Salam, Barkat, Rafiq, Jabbar, and Shafiur Rahman were killed, and their sacrifice became a lasting symbol of linguistic rights. Their memory is honoured at the Shaheed Minar, the Martyrs' Monument in Dhaka. Years later, the world recognised this sacrifice. On 17 November 1999, UNESCO proclaimed 21 February as International Mother Language Day, and it has been observed around the world since 2000. People mark the day by visiting Shaheed Minar, placing flowers, arranging discussions, holding cultural programmes, and reading poetry. The observance reminds us that language carries history, identity, and knowledge. We should respect our mother tongue, develop it through reading and writing, and show equal respect for other languages. Protecting linguistic diversity helps communities live with dignity and understanding. In Bangladesh, the day begins in the early hours, when people walk barefoot to the Shaheed Minar with flowers in their hands. They sing 'Amar Bhaiyer Rokte Rangano Ekushey February', the song written in memory of the martyrs, and the whole nation remembers the price paid for Bangla. The day teaches us that a mother tongue is not only a means of communication; it is the voice of a people's history, poetry, and dreams. International Mother Language Day Paragraph in 300 Words Best for SSC and HSC. International Mother Language Day is observed on 21 February to honour the languages spoken by people around the world. The day also recalls the language movement in Bangladesh, when students and citizens protested in 1952 for the right to use Bangla as a state language. At that time, most people of the country spoke Bangla, yet the central government had declared that Urdu alone would be the state language. On 21 February 1952, students of the University of Dhaka defied a ban on public gatherings and marched to demand recognition for Bangla. Near Dhaka Medical College, police opened fire on the peaceful procession. Salam, Barkat, Rafiq, Jabbar, and Shafiur Rahman were killed, and many others were injured. Their sacrifice became a lasting symbol of linguistic rights, and within a few years Bangla was recognised as an official language. Years later, the world recognised this sacrifice. On 17 November 1999, UNESCO proclaimed 21 February as International Mother Language Day, and it has been observed around the world since 2000. People mark the day by visiting Shaheed Minar, placing flowers, arranging discussions, holding cultural programmes, and reading poetry. The observance reminds us that language carries history, identity, and knowledge. We should respect our mother tongue, develop it through reading and writing, and show equal respect for other languages. Protecting linguistic diversity helps communities live with dignity and understanding. Students who protested in 1952 showed that a people who love their language will also defend their dignity. Today, when we speak Bangla freely, we should remember that this freedom was bought with blood. The best way to honour the martyrs is to use Bangla correctly, to read Bangla books, and to teach our children to love their mother tongue while respecting every other language of the world. plainContent: This is the completing story of a lion and a mouse, written for Class 6 to 10, SSC and HSC students. The given beginning is: "Once, a lion was sleeping under a tree in a forest. A little mouse came out of its hole and began to run over the lion's body." Read the complete story below, then learn the moral, the Bangla meaning and the important words at the end. A Lion and a Mouse (Complete Story) Once, a lion was sleeping under a tree in a forest. A little mouse came out of its hole and began to run over the lion's body. The mouse was playing happily and did not notice that the lion had woken up. Suddenly, the lion caught the little creature with his strong paw and prepared to punish it. The mouse was very frightened. It begged for freedom in a trembling voice. "Please let me go, O King," it said. "I am very small, and I am not good food for you. If you spare my life, I may be able to help you someday." The lion laughed at the unlikely idea. How could such a small creature help the king of the forest? But the mouse looked so helpless that the lion felt pity. He opened his paw and let the mouse go. "Run away," he said, "and do not disturb my sleep again." The mouse thanked the lion again and again and ran back to its hole. The lion soon forgot the whole matter and went back to sleep. Days passed, and the forest returned to its usual calm. The lion hunted, rested, and walked through his territory without fear. He did not remember the small mouse at all. But the mouse remembered the lion's kindness and often told its family how the king of the forest had spared its life. Some time later, hunters came to the forest and set a strong net to catch the lion. That night, the lion walked into the trap. The ropes held him fast, and he could not free himself. He roared loudly in anger and fear, and his roar was heard far away. The little mouse heard the roar and hurried to the place. It saw the lion caught in the net and remembered the lion's kindness. Without wasting time, it began to gnaw through the ropes with its sharp teeth, one strand at a time. The work was slow, but the mouse did not stop. At last, the net was cut, and the lion was free. The lion thanked the mouse warmly. He understood that size does not determine usefulness. Everyone has abilities that may become valuable in an unexpected situation. Kindness also creates bonds that return when help is needed. From that day, the lion and the mouse became good friends. Moral Never despise a small friend; kindness is rarely wasted. Bangla Meaning of the Story গল্পটির বাংলা অর্থ একদিন একটি সিংহ বনের একটি গাছের নিচে ঘুমাচ্ছিল। একটি ছোট ইঁদুর তার গর্ত থেকে বের হয়ে সিংহের শরীরের উপর দৌড়াতে লাগল। সিংহ জেগে উঠে ইঁদুরটিকে ধরে ফেলল। ইঁদুর ভয়ে কাঁপতে কাঁপতে প্রাণভিক্ষা চাইল এবং বলল, একদিন হয়তো সে সিংহের উপকারে আসতে পারবে। সিংহ হাসলেও দয়া করে ইঁদুরটিকে ছেড়ে দিল। কিছুদিন পর শিকারিরা সিংহকে শক্ত জালে আটকে ফেলল। সিংহের গর্জন শুনে ইঁদুর ছুটে এলো এবং তার ধারালো দাঁত দিয়ে একটু একটু করে জালের দড়ি কেটে সিংহকে মুক্ত করল। তখন সিংহ বুঝল, ছোট বলে কাউকে তুচ্ছ করা উচিত নয়। দয়া কখনো বৃথা যায় না। এরপর বনে আবার শান্তি ফিরে এলো। সিংহ শিকার করত, বিশ্রাম নিত এবং নির্ভয়ে ঘুরে বেড়াত। সে ছোট ইঁদুরের কথা ভুলেই গিয়েছিল। কিন্তু ইঁদুর সিংহের দয়া ভোলেনি এবং প্রায়ই তার পরিবারকে বলত, বনের রাজা কীভাবে তার প্রাণ রক্ষা করেছিলেন। Important Word Meanings English Word Bangla Meaning Creature প্রাণী Trembling কাঁপতে থাকা Spare রেহাই দেওয়া Pity দয়া, করুণা Trap ফাঁদ Roar গর্জন Gnaw কুটকুট করে কাটা Strand সুতো, দড়ির অংশ Despise তুচ্ছ করা, ঘৃণা করা Unexpected অপ্রত্যাশিত Exam Tips Begin the story with the given beginning exactly as it is written in the question, then continue it in your own words. Keep the events in order: the lion catches the mouse, the mouse begs for freedom, the lion frees it, the hunters trap the lion, and the mouse cuts the net. Write in the past tense, because the story happened in the past. Do not change the main idea of the story. The mouse must save the lion by its own small ability. End the story with the moral in a separate short paragraph, as shown above. Use the lion's and the mouse's feelings in your sentences. Words like frightened, pity and grateful make the story lively. title: Letter How to improve English
excerpt: On this page you will find a letter about how to improve English, written in simple English for Class 6 to 10, SSC and HSC students. It gives the format of a
plainContent: On this page you will find a letter about how to improve English, written in simple English for Class 6 to 10, SSC and HSC students. It gives the format of a personal letter, a full example letter, its Bangla meaning, important word meanings and exam tips. You can learn the letter for your examination and also follow its advice to improve your English at the same time. Format Your address at the top of the letter, on the right or left side as your teacher advises. The date below your address, so the reader knows when you wrote the letter. A greeting or salutation, such as "Dear Tuhin," to the friend you are writing to. The body of the letter, in three or four short paragraphs, with your main ideas in order. A closing line, such as "With love," followed by your name at the end of the letter. Simple and correct English throughout, with short sentences that are easy to understand. Letter: How to Improve English (Example) Dear Tuhin, I hope you are well. Thank you for your letter. You asked me how I am improving my English, so I am writing to share the simple methods that are helping me most. English is important for our studies, for good jobs and for learning about the world, so I try to practise it a little every day instead of studying it only before an examination. First, I read something in English every day. I read a short story, a newspaper article or a lesson from my textbook, and I note down useful expressions, not only single words. Then I listen to clear English conversations and repeat the sentences aloud, so my pronunciation and speaking become better. I also speak in English with a friend for a few minutes every day, even if I make mistakes. Second, I write a little every day. I write a diary entry or a short paragraph, and then I check the spelling and grammar carefully. I keep a vocabulary notebook and try to use each new word in a sentence of my own, because a word is easy to remember when I use it myself. I use a dictionary when I do not know a word, but I do not memorise long lists without understanding them. When I make a mistake, I correct it and try again, because correction is a natural part of learning. I hope these ideas will help you too. Start with fifteen minutes a day, and increase the time slowly when you feel comfortable. With patience and regular practice, your reading, writing, listening and speaking will all become stronger. Please write back soon and tell me how your practice is going. With love, Mim Bangla Meaning ইংরেজি উন্নত করার চিঠির বাংলা অর্থ প্রিয় তুহিন, আশা করি তুমি ভালো আছো। তোমার চিঠির জন্য ধন্যবাদ। তুমি জানতে চেয়েছ আমি কীভাবে আমার ইংরেজি উন্নত করছি, তাই আমার সবচেয়ে কাজে লাগা সহজ উপায়গুলো জানিয়ে লিখছি। পড়াশোনা, ভালো চাকরি এবং পৃথিবী সম্পর্কে জানার জন্য ইংরেজি খুব গুরুত্বপূর্ণ। তাই আমি শুধু পরীক্ষার আগে নয়, প্রতিদিন একটু একটু করে ইংরেজি চর্চা করার চেষ্টা করি। প্রথমে আমি প্রতিদিন ইংরেজিতে কিছু পড়ি। আমি একটি ছোট গল্প, সংবাদপত্রের একটি প্রবন্ধ অথবা পাঠ্যবইয়ের একটি পাঠ পড়ি এবং শুধু আলাদা আলাদা শব্দ নয়, কাজের বাক্যাংশগুলো লিখে রাখি। তারপর আমি পরিষ্কার ইংরেজি কথোপকথন শুনি এবং বাক্যগুলো জোরে জোরে বলি, যাতে আমার উচ্চারণ ও কথা বলা ভালো হয়। আমি প্রতিদিন কয়েক মিনিট একজন বন্ধুর সঙ্গে ইংরেজিতে কথা বলি, ভুল হলেও থামি না। দ্বিতীয়ত, আমি প্রতিদিন একটু লিখি। আমি একটি ডায়েরি লিখি অথবা একটি ছোট অনুচ্ছেদ লিখি, তারপর বানান ও ব্যাকরণ ভালোভাবে দেখে নিই। আমি একটি শব্দভান্ডারের খাতা রাখি এবং প্রতিটি নতুন শব্দ নিজের বাক্যে ব্যবহার করার চেষ্টা করি, কারণ নিজে ব্যবহার করলে শব্দ মনে রাখা সহজ হয়। অজানা শব্দের জন্য আমি অভিধান ব্যবহার করি, কিন্তু না বুঝে লম্বা তালিকা মুখস্থ করি না। ভুল করলে তা ঠিক করে আবার চেষ্টা করি, কারণ ভুল থেকে শেখা শেখারই একটি স্বাভাবিক অংশ। আশা করি এই ধারণাগুলো তোমারও কাজে আসবে। প্রতিদিন পনেরো মিনিট দিয়ে শুরু করো এবং স্বাচ্ছন্দ্য বোধ করলে ধীরে ধীরে সময় বাড়াও। ধৈর্য ও নিয়মিত চর্চায় তোমার পড়া, লেখা, শোনা ও বলা—সবই শক্তিশালী হবে। শীঘ্রই উত্তর লিখে জানিও তোমার চর্চা কেমন চলছে। Important Word Meanings English Word Bangla Meaning Improve উন্নত করা Regular নিয়মিত Expression বাক্যাংশ Pronunciation উচ্চারণ Confidence আত্মবিশ্বাস Vocabulary শব্দভান্ডার Dictionary অভিধান Memorise মুখস্থ করা Embarrassed লজ্জিত Patience ধৈর্য Exam Tips Learn the format first: address, date, salutation, body in three or four paragraphs, and a closing line with your name. Marks are given for a correct format as well as for good English. Do not memorise the whole letter word by word. Learn the main points — reading daily, listening and speaking, writing daily, and using new words — and write them in your own simple sentences in the examination hall. Keep your sentences short and correct. One long and confusing sentence is worse than two short and clear sentences, and short sentences are easier to write without grammar mistakes. Use the Bangla meaning to understand the letter fully before you memorise the English version, so you can change a sentence in your own words if you forget the exact wording. Revise the letter once the night before the examination and read it again in the morning, instead of trying to learn it for the first time in the hall. title: Letter about Brilliant Success
excerpt: On this page you will find a letter about brilliant success, written in simple English for Class 6 to 10, SSC and HSC students. It gives the format of a
plainContent: On this page you will find a letter about brilliant success, written in simple English for Class 6 to 10, SSC and HSC students. It gives the format of a personal letter, a full example letter congratulating a friend on an excellent SSC result, its Bangla meaning, important word meanings and exam tips. You can learn the letter for your examination and use it to congratulate a friend in real life too. Format Your address at the top of the letter, on the right or left side as your teacher advises. The date below your address, so the reader knows when you wrote the letter. A greeting or salutation, such as "Dear Tanvir," to the friend you are writing to. The body of the letter, in three or four short paragraphs, with your congratulations, the reason for them, and your good wishes for the future. A closing line, such as "With best wishes," followed by your name at the end of the letter. Simple and correct English throughout, with short sentences that are easy to understand. Letter: Congratulations on Brilliant Success (Example) Dear Tanvir, I was delighted to hear that you achieved an excellent result in the SSC examination. Please accept my warm congratulations. Your success is the reward for your regular study, careful preparation and strong determination. You studied every day, followed your routine, and never gave up even when a lesson was difficult. I am very happy for you, and I know how proud your parents and teachers must feel today. Your result has brought pride and happiness to your whole family. Your parents worked hard for you, and your teachers guided you with care, so this success belongs to their love and support as well as to your own effort. Your friends are also glad to see you do so well. A good result like this does not come by luck alone; it comes from honest work, patience and discipline over a long time. Do not become careless after this achievement. Success is only the beginning of a longer journey, and the next stage will need the same hard work. Continue learning with the same discipline, choose your next course thoughtfully, and set a clear goal for your future. Take advice from your parents and teachers before you decide, because a good decision now will help you for many years. I am sure that your honesty and hard work will help you reach an even brighter goal. Keep your good habits, stay humble, and help your classmates who are still trying to improve. I pray that you will do even better in the HSC examination and in your life ahead. Please convey my respects to your parents. With best wishes, Rahim Bangla Meaning অসাধারণ সাফল্যের চিঠির বাংলা অর্থ প্রিয় তানভীর, এসএসসি পরীক্ষায় তুমি চমৎকার ফলাফল করেছ শুনে আমি খুব আনন্দিত হয়েছি। আমার আন্তরিক অভিনন্দন গ্রহণ করো। তোমার এই সাফল্য তোমার নিয়মিত পড়াশোনা, যত্নশীল প্রস্তুতি ও দৃঢ় সংকল্পের পুরস্কার। তুমি প্রতিদিন পড়েছ, নিজের রুটিন মেনে চলেছ এবং কোনো পাঠ কঠিন হলেও হাল ছাড়োনি। আমি তোমার জন্য খুব খুশি, আর জানি আজ তোমার বাবা-মা ও শিক্ষকেরা কতটা গর্বিত। তোমার ফলাফল তোমার পুরো পরিবারের জন্য গর্ব ও আনন্দ বয়ে এনেছে। তোমার বাবা-মা তোমার জন্য অনেক কষ্ট করেছেন এবং তোমার শিক্ষকেরা যত্নে তোমাকে পথ দেখিয়েছেন, তাই এই সাফল্য তোমার নিজের চেষ্টার পাশাপাশি তাঁদের ভালোবাসা ও সহযোগিতারও ফসল। তোমার বন্ধুরাও তোমার ভালো ফল দেখে খুশি। এমন ভালো ফল শুধু ভাগ্যে আসে না; তা আসে দীর্ঘদিনের সৎ পরিশ্রম, ধৈর্য ও শৃঙ্খলা থেকে। এই অর্জনের পর অসতর্ক হয়ো না। সাফল্য কেবল একটি দীর্ঘ যাত্রার শুরু, আর পরের ধাপেও একই পরিশ্রম দরকার হবে। একই শৃঙ্খলা নিয়ে পড়াশোনা চালিয়ে যাও, ভেবেচিন্তে তোমার পরের পাঠক্রমটি বেছে নাও এবং ভবিষ্যতের জন্য একটি স্পষ্ট লক্ষ্য ঠিক করো। সিদ্ধান্ত নেওয়ার আগে বাবা-মা ও শিক্ষকদের পরামর্শ নাও, কারণ এখনকার একটি ভালো সিদ্ধান্ত অনেক বছর ধরে তোমাকে সাহায্য করবে। আমি নিশ্চিত, তোমার সততা ও কঠোর পরিশ্রম তোমাকে আরও উজ্জ্বল লক্ষ্যে পৌঁছাতে সাহায্য করবে। তোমার ভালো অভ্যাসগুলো ধরে রাখো, বিনয়ী থেকো এবং যেসব সহপাঠী এখনো উন্নতি করার চেষ্টা করছে তাদের সাহায্য করো। আমি প্রার্থনা করি, এইচএসসি পরীক্ষায় ও সামনের জীবনে তুমি আরও ভালো করবে। তোমার বাবা-মাকে আমার শ্রদ্ধা জানিও। Important Word Meanings English Word Bangla Meaning Delighted আনন্দিত Congratulations অভিনন্দন Achievement অর্জন Determination দৃঢ় সংকল্প Pride গর্ব Discipline শৃঙ্খলা Thoughtfully ভেবেচিন্তে Humble বিনয়ী Honesty সততা Brilliant উজ্জ্বল Exam Tips Learn the format first: address, date, salutation, body in three or four paragraphs, and a closing line with your name. Marks are given for a correct format as well as for good English. Remember the three parts of the body: congratulate your friend, explain why the success is deserved, and give good wishes and advice for the future. Keep these ideas in order so the letter reads naturally. Do not memorise the whole letter word by word. title: Letter about Preparation for Exam
excerpt: On this page you will find a letter about preparation for the examination, written in simple English for Class 6 to 10, SSC and HSC students. It gives the
plainContent: On this page you will find a letter about preparation for the examination, written in simple English for Class 6 to 10, SSC and HSC students. It gives the format of a personal letter, a full example letter describing how the writer is preparing for an examination, its Bangla meaning, important word meanings and exam tips. You can learn the letter for your examination and follow its study plan in your own preparation too. Format Your address at the top of the letter, on the right or left side as your teacher advises. The date below your address, so the reader knows when you wrote the letter. A greeting or salutation, such as "Dear Shila," to the friend you are writing to. The body of the letter, in three or four short paragraphs, describing your timetable, your revision, and your daily habits. A closing line, such as "Yours affectionately," followed by your name at the end of the letter. Simple and correct English throughout, with short sentences that are easy to understand. Letter: How I Am Preparing for the Examination (Example) Dear Shila, You asked about my examination preparation, so I am writing to tell you how I am getting ready. I made a timetable that divides each day into short study sessions and includes time for sleep, meals and exercise. I study the difficult subjects when my mind is fresh in the morning, and I keep the easier lessons for the afternoon. I follow the timetable every day, because a good plan is useful only when it is followed regularly. I am reviewing the difficult chapters first, and I am practising questions under time limits so that I can finish the paper in the examination hall. I keep a notebook of my mistakes, and I look at it before every test, because the same mistake should not happen twice. I also discuss confusing topics with my teachers instead of memorising blindly, and they explain the ideas in a simple way that I can remember. Each week I revise earlier lessons so that they do not fade from my memory. I read my notes again, solve a few old questions, and mark the parts I still find hard. I am trying to remain calm and avoid wasting time on my phone, because too much time on the phone breaks my concentration. I sleep on time and eat well, since a tired mind cannot learn properly. Your advice to study consistently has been very helpful to me, and I thank you for it. I feel more confident now than I did a month ago, though I still have much to revise. Please pray for me, and write back to tell me how your own preparation is going. I hope we both do well in the examination. A Street Hawker Paragraph in 150 Words Best for Class 6–7. A street hawker sells goods from a basket, cart, or temporary stand instead of a permanent shop. Hawkers may offer fruit, vegetables, snacks, clothes, toys, household items, or newspapers. Their flexible prices and convenient locations make them useful to busy customers, especially in crowded neighbourhoods. Most hawkers work long hours in sun and rain and have little protection from eviction, illness, or loss of stock. Food sellers also face the responsibility of keeping products covered and using clean water. Unplanned stalls can narrow pavements and create waste, so fair rules are needed. Street hawkers contribute to the local economy, and orderly planning can support both their livelihood and the public's right to move safely. Customers should bargain fairly, avoid littering, and choose safe food, because a hawker's small income depends on honest trade. With fair rules, small trade can benefit everyone in the city. plainContent: On this page you will find a Life of a Farmer paragraph in 150, 250 and 300 words for Class 6 to 12, SSC and HSC. The short version is best for junior classes, the longer versions are best for SSC and HSC. A Bangla meaning, important word meanings and exam tips are given at the end. The Life of a Farmer Paragraph in 150 Words Best for Class 6–7. A farmer grows crops and raises animals that help feed society. In Bangladesh many farmers cultivate rice, wheat, pulses, vegetables, jute, sugarcane, and other produce. Their work begins early, when they prepare soil, sow seeds, manage water, remove weeds, and protect plants from pests. Farming demands patience and physical effort. A farmer may work under strong sun or heavy rain and wait months before knowing whether the harvest will succeed. Floods, drought, cyclones, disease, and insects can destroy crops. When the harvest is good, the farmer supplies food to markets and earns money for the family; when it fails, debt and hardship may follow. Farmers need fair prices, quality seed, affordable credit, irrigation, and storage. Their contribution is fundamental to national life, so agriculture deserves sustained public support. Better roads and markets can reduce waste between field and consumer, and crop insurance can protect farmers from a bad season. The Life of a Farmer Paragraph in 250 Words Best for Class 8–10 and SSC. A farmer grows crops and raises animals that help feed society. In Bangladesh many farmers cultivate rice, wheat, pulses, vegetables, jute, sugarcane, and other produce. Their work begins early, when they prepare soil, sow seeds, manage water, remove weeds, and protect plants from pests. Farming demands patience and physical effort, because the result of months of work is known only at harvest time. A farmer may work under strong sun or heavy rain and wait months before knowing whether the harvest will succeed. Floods, drought, cyclones, disease, and insects can destroy crops. When the harvest is good, the farmer supplies food to markets and earns money for the family; when it fails, debt and hardship may follow. Many farmers borrow money to buy seed and fertiliser, so a bad season can leave them in debt for years. Farmers need fair prices, quality seed, affordable credit, irrigation, storage, crop insurance, and access to agricultural advice. Better roads and markets can reduce waste between field and consumer. Respecting farmers also means avoiding food waste and understanding the labour behind every meal. Their contribution is fundamental to national life, so agriculture deserves sustained public support and modern, climate-resilient methods. In recent years, many farmers have started using mobile phones to check market prices and weather forecasts, and this simple technology helps them sell at a better price. Young educated farmers are also trying new methods, such as drip irrigation and organic fertiliser, which save water and keep the soil healthy. If the country supports these efforts, agriculture can become both modern and profitable. The Life of a Farmer Paragraph in 300 Words Best for SSC and HSC. A farmer may work under strong sun or heavy rain and wait months before knowing whether the harvest will succeed. Floods, drought, cyclones, disease, and insects can destroy crops. When the harvest is good, the farmer supplies food to markets and earns money for the family; when it fails, debt and hardship may follow. Many farmers borrow money to buy seed and fertiliser, so a bad season can leave them in debt for years. Yet they return to the field each season, because farming is not only their work but also their way of life. Farmers need fair prices, quality seed, affordable credit, irrigation, storage, crop insurance, and access to agricultural advice. Better roads and markets can reduce waste between field and consumer, so that more of what is grown reaches the people who need it. Respecting farmers also means avoiding food waste and understanding the labour behind every meal. Their contribution is fundamental to national life, so agriculture deserves sustained public support and modern, climate-resilient methods. A nation that forgets its farmers forgets the source of its food. Every meal we eat begins in a farmer's field, and remembering this simple truth is the first step towards respecting farmers. Let us waste less food and thank the hands that grow it. That is the least we can do. My Village Paragraph in 150 Words Best for Class 6–7. My village is a quiet community where people live close to fields, ponds, trees, and one another. It is not a large place, yet its green landscape and friendly people make it special to me. Farmers form the largest group, while teachers, shopkeepers, office workers, and fishers also contribute to village life. The village has primary and secondary schools, a market, a health centre, a post office, and places of worship. A paved road joins it to the main highway, and smaller roads connect the neighbourhoods. The fields become bright with crops during the growing season. Fresh vegetables, fish, milk, and clean air are among the benefits of rural life. I love my village because it is beautiful, cooperative, and closely connected to nature. People help one another in times of need, and neighbours know each other by name. This closeness is the real beauty of village life. My Village Paragraph in 250 Words Best for Class 8–10 and SSC. My village is a quiet community where people live close to fields, ponds, trees, and one another. It is not a large place, yet its green landscape and friendly people make it special to me. People of different religions live together respectfully and share one another's joys and difficulties. Fresh vegetables, fish, milk, and clean air are among the benefits of rural life. Although modern facilities are increasing, the village still retains its calm character. I hope to help its people prosper while preserving its peaceful environment. In the evening, children play in the open ground while older people sit under the big trees and talk about the day. Festivals and weddings bring the whole village together, and no one is left out of the celebration. Life in a village moves slowly, but it is full of warmth and friendship that city life often lacks. My Village Paragraph in 300 Words Best for SSC and HSC. My village is a quiet community where people live close to fields, ponds, trees, and one another. It is not a large place, yet its green landscape and friendly people make it special to me. Farmers form the largest group, while teachers, shopkeepers, office workers, fishers, and other professionals also contribute to village life. People of different religions live together respectfully and share one another's joys and difficulties. In my village, a neighbour's problem is everyone's problem, and a wedding or a festival is celebrated by the whole village. The village has primary and secondary schools, a market, a health centre, a post office, and places of worship. A paved road joins it to the main highway, and smaller roads connect the neighbourhoods. The fields become bright with crops during the growing season, and a canal, shady trees, gardens, and open sky add to the scenery. Fresh vegetables, fish, milk, and clean air are among the benefits of rural life. In the morning, birds sing and farmers go to the fields, and in the evening, children play in the open ground. Although modern facilities are increasing, the village still retains its calm character. Electricity, mobile phones, and better roads have reached us, but people still help one another in times of need, and neighbours know each other by name. I love my village because it is beautiful, cooperative, and closely connected to nature. I hope to help its people prosper while preserving its peaceful environment, so that the next generation can also grow up in this calm and green place. Many people who move to the city for work still dream of their village, and they return home for festivals and holidays. The village lives in their hearts wherever they go. I am proud of my village. Bangla Meaning of My Village Paragraph আমার গ্রাম অনুচ্ছেদের বাংলা অর্থ আমার গ্রাম একটি শান্ত জনপদ, যেখানে মানুষ মাঠ, পুকুর, গাছপালা ও একে অপরের কাছাকাছি বাস করে। এটি বড় জায়গা নয়, তবুও এর সবুজ প্রকৃতি ও বন্ধুসুলভ মানুষের কারণে এটি আমার কাছে বিশেষ। কৃষকরাই সবচেয়ে বড় দল, আর শিক্ষক, দোকানদার, অফিস কর্মী ও জেলেরাও গ্রামের জীবনে অবদান রাখে। গ্রামে প্রাথমিক ও মাধ্যমিক বিদ্যালয়, বাজার, স্বাস্থ্যকেন্দ্র, ডাকঘর ও উপাসনালয় আছে। পাকা রাস্তা গ্রামকে মূল সড়কের সঙ্গে যুক্ত করেছে এবং ছোট রাস্তাগুলো পাড়াগুলোকে সংযুক্ত করেছে। চাষের মৌসুমে মাঠ ফসলে উজ্জ্বল হয়ে ওঠে। তাজা শাকসবজি, মাছ, দুধ ও নির্মল বাতাস গ্রামীণ জীবনের সুবিধা। আমি আমার গ্রামকে ভালোবাসি, কারণ এটি সুন্দর, সহযোগিতাপূর্ণ এবং প্রকৃতির সঙ্গে ঘনিষ্ঠভাবে যুক্ত। Important Word Meanings English Word Bangla Meaning Village গ্রাম Pond পুকুর Field মাঠ Neighbour প্রতিবেশী Peaceful শান্ত Cooperative সহযোগিতামূলক Scenery দৃশ্য Market বাজার Worship উপাসনা Prosper সমৃদ্ধ হওয়া Exam Tips Choose the version that matches your class: 150 words for Class 6–7, 250 words for Class 8–10 and SSC, 300 words for SSC and HSC. If the question asks for your own village, replace the general details with your village's real name, schools, river or pond, and main occupations. Do not memorise the whole paragraph word by word. Learn the main points — people, facilities, nature, and why you love it — and write them in your own sentences. Use the Bangla meaning to understand difficult words first. title: Importance of games and sports Dialogue
excerpt: This dialogue is about the importance of games and sports. It is written for Class 6 to 10, SSC and HSC students. The exam question is usually: "Write a
plainContent: This dialogue is about the importance of games and sports. It is written for Class 6 to 10, SSC and HSC students. The exam question is usually: "Write a dialogue between two friends about the importance of games and sports." Read the dialogue below, then learn the Bangla meaning and the important words at the end. The dialogue uses simple English, so you can learn it easily and rewrite it in your own words in the examination. Dialogue: Importance of Games and Sports Siam: I spend almost all my free time studying. Is playing games really necessary? Tania: Yes, it is. Games and sports make the body strong and the mind fresh. A student who never plays becomes tired and dull. Siam: But my parents want me to study all the time. They say games waste time. Tania: Study is important, but only study is not enough. Our body needs movement just as our mind needs rest. A short game after study can help us return to our books with more energy. Siam: Do games help with schoolwork too? Tania: They do. Regular play improves concentration, discipline and teamwork. In a team game, we learn to follow rules, to work with others and to accept both victory and defeat. Siam: That is true. When we lost the football match last month, I felt very bad at first. Tania: And then you practised harder and played better in the next match. That is what sports teach us — not to give up after a failure. Siam: Some students play for hours and forget their lessons completely. Tania: That is the other extreme. Balance is important. A timetable can give time to study, sleep, exercise and recreation. We should play for a fixed time and then stop. Siam: What kind of games are best for students? Tania: Outdoor games like football, cricket and badminton are very good because they give exercise in the open air. Indoor games like chess and carrom can also sharpen the mind. Siam: Our school has a small playground but not enough equipment. Tania: We can ask our teachers to arrange more equipment. We can also use the field in the morning before classes begin. Siam: Do indoor games help us too? Tania: They help in a different way. Chess teaches us to think ahead, and carrom improves focus. But they do not give exercise to the body. Siam: So we need both kinds? Tania: Yes. Outdoor games make the body strong, and indoor games make the mind sharp. A student should try both. Siam: I think I will join the school cricket practice this afternoon. Tania: Good choice. A healthy student needs both a trained mind and an active body. Games and sports give us both. Bangla Meaning of the Dialogue সংলাপটির বাংলা অর্থ সিয়াম প্রায় সব অবসর সময় পড়াশোনায় কাটায়। সে জানতে চায়, খেলাধুলা কি সত্যিই দরকারি। তানিয়া বলে, খেলাধুলা শরীরকে শক্তিশালী করে এবং মনকে সতেজ রাখে। শুধু পড়াশোনা করলেই চলে না; শরীরেরও ব্যায়াম দরকার। পড়ার পর অল্প সময় খেললে মন আবার পড়ায় ফিরতে পারে। নিয়মিত খেলাধুলা মনোযোগ, শৃঙ্খলা, দলগত কাজ এবং আত্মবিশ্বাস বাড়ায়। দলীয় খেলায় আমরা নিয়ম মানতে শিখি এবং জয়-পরাজয় মেনে নিতে শিখি। তবে ঘণ্টার পর ঘণ্টা খেলাও ঠিক নয় — ভারসাম্য দরকার। রুটিন করে পড়া, ঘুম, ব্যায়াম ও খেলার সময় ঠিক করতে হবে। ফুটবল, ক্রিকেট, ব্যাডমিন্টনের মতো বাইরের খেলা শরীরের জন্য ভালো, আর দাবা-ক্যারামের মতো ঘরের খেলা মনকে তীক্ষ্ণ করে। শেষে সিয়াম স্কুলের ক্রিকেট অনুশীলনে যোগ দেওয়ার সিদ্ধান্ত নেয়। সংলাপের শেষের দিকে সিয়াম জানতে চায়, ঘরের খেলা কি একইভাবে সাহায্য করে। তানিয়া বলে, দাবা আমাদের আগে থেকে ভাবতে ও পরিকল্পনা করতে শেখায়, আর ক্যারাম মনোযোগ ও ধৈর্য বাড়ায়। তবে এগুলো শরীরের ব্যায়াম দেয় না। তাই বাইরের খেলা শরীরকে শক্তিশালী করে, আর ঘরের খেলা মনকে তীক্ষ্ণ করে — একজন ছাত্রের দুটোই দরকার। সিয়াম আরও জানতে চায়, স্কুলে খেলার জন্য বেশি সময় দেওয়া উচিত কি না। তানিয়া বলে, প্রতিটি স্কুলে প্রতিদিন একটি খেলার পিরিয়ড থাকা উচিত এবং ছাত্রদের জন্য একটি ভালো খেলার মাঠ থাকা উচিত। Important Word Meanings English Word Bangla Meaning Concentration মনোযোগ Discipline শৃঙ্খলা Teamwork দলগত কাজ Victory জয় Defeat পরাজয় Recreation বিনোদন Balance ভারসাম্য Equipment সরঞ্জাম Practice অনুশীলন Active সক্রিয় Exam Tips Write the dialogue as a conversation, not as a paragraph. Put the speaker's name and a colon before each line. Keep the language simple and natural, the way students really speak to each other. Show both sides of the topic: the benefits of games and sports, and the danger of playing too much. Give the dialogue a clear ending — a decision or an agreement — instead of stopping suddenly. Learn the important words from the table so that you can write the dialogue in your own sentences in the exam. Before the examination, do not memorise the dialogue word by word. Practise it with a friend so that it sounds like a real conversation. If the question asks for a dialogue between two friends, use two names. Do not write the dialogue as a paragraph or an essay. title: Morning Walk Dialogue for Class 6,7,8, SSC, HSC
excerpt: This dialogue is about the benefits of a morning walk. It is written for Class 6 to 10, SSC and HSC students. The exam question is usually: "Write a dialogue
plainContent: This dialogue is about the benefits of a morning walk. It is written for Class 6 to 10, SSC and HSC students. The exam question is usually: "Write a dialogue between two friends about the benefits of a morning walk." Read the dialogue below, then learn the Bangla meaning and the important words at the end. The dialogue uses simple English, so you can learn it easily and rewrite it in your own words in the examination. Dialogue: Morning Walk Rony: You look energetic today. Did you exercise? Lima: I took a brisk walk before breakfast. The cool air made it easy to continue. Rony: What benefits do you notice from a morning walk? Lima: Walking improves fitness, supports the heart, refreshes the mind, and helps me begin my studies with concentration. Rony: Do we need special equipment for a morning walk? Lima: Comfortable shoes and a safe route are enough. We should start gently, keep a steady pace, and drink water after the walk. Rony: I usually wake late and feel tired all day. I never get time for a walk. Lima: Try going to bed on time and walking for twenty minutes at first. You do not need to walk for hours to feel the benefit. Rony: Is it safe to walk alone in the early morning? Lima: It is safer to walk with a friend or a family member. Choose a road away from heavy traffic and avoid dark, lonely places. Rony: What else can we do during a morning walk? Lima: We can enjoy the fresh air, the birds and the rising sun. Some people listen to the news or revise a lesson in their mind while walking. Rony: That sounds pleasant. I have been wasting my mornings in bed for a long time. Lima: A morning walk is a simple habit, but it changes the whole day. The body becomes active, the mind becomes calm, and study becomes easier. Rony: How long should a morning walk be? Lima: Twenty to thirty minutes is enough for a student. We should not tire ourselves before school. Rony: What should we wear for a morning walk? Lima: Light, comfortable clothes and shoes that fit well. Rony: Does a morning walk help with study? Lima: Yes. After a walk, the mind is fresh and the memory works better. Many students find that lessons learned in the morning stay in the mind longer. Rony: I have heard that morning air is cleaner than the air later in the day. Lima: That is true. There is less dust and smoke in the early morning, and the air feels fresh after the night. Rony: I will join you tomorrow, provided we choose a safe road away from traffic. Lima: Good. We will meet at six in the morning near the school gate. Bring a water bottle and wear comfortable shoes. Bangla Meaning of the Dialogue সংলাপটির বাংলা অর্থ রনি দেখে লিমা আজ খুব চনমনে। লিমা বলে, সে নাশতার আগে দ্রুত হেঁটেছে। ঠান্ডা বাতাসে হাঁটতে ভালো লেগেছে। সকালের হাঁটা শরীর ভালো রাখে, হৃদয়ের জন্য উপকারী, মনকে সতেজ করে এবং পড়াশোনায় মনোযোগ বাড়ায়। সকালের হাঁটার জন্য বিশেষ কিছু লাগে না — আরামদায়ক জুতা আর নিরাপদ রাস্তাই যথেষ্ট। ধীরে শুরু করে নিয়মিত গতিতে হাঁটতে হয় এবং পরে পানি পান করতে হয়। রনি দেরিতে ঘুম থেকে ওঠে বলে সারাদিন ক্লান্ত থাকে। লিমা তাকে সময়মতো ঘুমাতে এবং প্রথমে বিশ মিনিট হাঁটতে বলে। বন্ধুর সঙ্গে হাঁটলে নিরাপদ হয়। শেষে রনি পরদিন সকালে লিমার সঙ্গে হাঁটতে যাওয়ার সিদ্ধান্ত নেয়। লিমা আরও বলে, বিশ থেকে ত্রিশ মিনিট হাঁটাই একজন ছাত্রের জন্য যথেষ্ট। হাঁটার জন্য হালকা আরামদায়ক পোশাক ও ভালো জুতা দরকার। শীতকালে গরম সোয়েটার পরা উচিত। হাঁটার পর মন সতেজ থাকে এবং স্মৃতিশক্তি ভালো কাজ করে। সকালে শেখা পাঠ মনে থাকে বেশি। সকালের বাতাস দিনের পরের সময়ের চেয়ে পরিষ্কার থাকে, কারণ তখন ধুলো ও ধোঁয়া কম থাকে। Important Word Meanings English Word Bangla Meaning Brisk দ্রুত, চটপটে Energetic উদ্যমী Fitness সুস্থতা Concentration মনোযোগ Steady স্থির, নিয়মিত Pace গতি Refresh সতেজ করা Benefit উপকার Habit অভ্যাস Pleasant আনন্দদায়ক Exam Tips Write the dialogue as a conversation, not as a paragraph. Put the speaker's name and a colon before each line. Keep the language simple and natural, the way two friends really talk in the morning. Include clear benefits of a morning walk — health, fresh air, a calm mind and better study — instead of writing only general sentences. Give the dialogue a clear ending, such as a plan to walk together the next morning. Learn the important words from the table so that you can write the dialogue in your own sentences in the exam. Practise the dialogue with a classmate before the exam so that the questions and answers sound natural. In the examination, write the dialogue in the present tense, because the two friends are talking about a daily habit. title: Proper Use of Time dialogue
excerpt: This dialogue is about the proper use of time. It is written for Class 6 to 10, SSC and HSC students. The exam question is usually: "Write a dialogue between
plainContent: This dialogue is about the proper use of time. It is written for Class 6 to 10, SSC and HSC students. The exam question is usually: "Write a dialogue between two friends about the proper use of time." Read the dialogue below, then learn the Bangla meaning and the important words at the end. The dialogue uses simple English, so you can learn it easily and rewrite it in your own words in the examination. Dialogue: Proper Use of Time Sajib: You seem relaxed before the examination. Have you finished your revision? Nayeem: I made a timetable last month and followed it most days. I divide large chapters into small tasks, so the work never feels too heavy. Sajib: I often lose an hour to my phone and then try to study late at night. Nayeem: A schedule helps. Keep the phone away during study periods and set a clear stopping time. Short breaks make the work easier. Sajib: Do you study all day without any rest? Nayeem: No. I leave time for sleep, meals, exercise, prayer, and family. Using time well means giving each duty its proper place, not remaining busy every minute. Sajib: What if an unexpected task appears and breaks the plan? Nayeem: I keep some free space in the plan and complete the most important work first. At night I check what was done and adjust tomorrow's list. Sajib: I start many things but finish very few of them. Nayeem: That happens when we try to do everything at once. Choose one task, finish it, and then move to the next. Small finished tasks build confidence. Sajib: I also waste time deciding what to study first. Nayeem: Write the list the night before. In the morning you will know exactly where to begin, and you will not waste the first hour in confusion. Sajib: I understand. Time cannot be stored for later. Nayeem: Exactly. Once a day passes, we can only learn from it. Good habits turn small periods into steady progress. Sajib: Do you use a diary or a phone to keep your timetable? Nayeem: I use a small notebook. I write tomorrow's tasks before going to bed, and I tick each one when it is finished. Sajib: That must take extra time. Nayeem: Those few minutes save much more time the next morning, because I do not waste time deciding what to do first. Sajib: What about time with friends? Should we stop meeting them? Nayeem: No. Meeting friends is also important, but it needs a fixed time. If we meet for half an hour after lunch, it refreshes the mind without harming study. Sajib: From today I will make a simple timetable and follow it for one week. Nayeem: Good. Start small and keep it regular. A student who values time can finish his work without hurry and still enjoy his free time. Importance of Learning English Paragraph in 150 Words Best for Class 6–7. English is an international language. It is used in education, science, business, travel, technology and communication all over the world. It is the main language of the internet, international meetings and most scientific books. A student who knows English can read more books, follow online lessons and talk with people from many countries. English is also useful for higher study and for many careers. Students can apply for scholarships, read research papers and work with people from other countries. In Bangladesh, good English helps in jobs, examinations and interviews. Many good books and courses are available only in English. Learning English takes regular practice. Students should read simple texts, listen carefully, speak without fear and write a little every day. Mistakes are a natural part of learning. English should not replace our mother tongue; it should add another useful way to express ourselves. Importance of Learning English Paragraph in 250 Words Best for Class 8–10 and SSC. A Book Fair Paragraph in 150 Words Best for Class 6–7. A book fair is a temporary marketplace where publishers, booksellers, writers and readers meet. Rows of colourful stalls in one place display storybooks, novels, science books, biographies, dictionaries and works by local authors. Visitors can look at new books, compare prices and meet writers. The fair is enjoyable, but its greatest value is educational. It introduces children to many kinds of reading and encourages families to make books part of everyday life. A child who loves books becomes a thoughtful person. Publishers also use the fair to present new ideas and support young writers. In Bangladesh, the Amar Ekushey Book Fair is held in Dhaka in February by Bangla Academy. It honours the martyrs of the Language Movement of 1952. When I visit a fair, I make a list before entering so that excitement does not make me waste money. A well-organised book fair combines recreation with learning. title: The Ant and the Grasshopper Completing Story
excerpt: This is the completing story of the ant and the grasshopper, written for Class 6 to 10, SSC and HSC students. The given beginning is: "Once there lived an ant
plainContent: This is the completing story of the ant and the grasshopper, written for Class 6 to 10, SSC and HSC students. The given beginning is: "Once there lived an ant and a grasshopper in a field. The ant was hard-working, but the grasshopper loved to sing and play all day." Read the complete story below, then learn the moral, the Bangla meaning and the important words at the end. The story shows why we should prepare in good times. The Ant and the Grasshopper (Complete Story) Once there lived an ant and a grasshopper in a field. The ant was hard-working, but the grasshopper loved to sing and play all day. Throughout the warm months, the ant carried grains to a dry store beneath a tree. It worked a little every day, and it did not refuse rest or happiness; it simply prepared before the weather changed. Nearby, the grasshopper spent the days singing and resting in the sun. One day, the ant invited him to gather food before winter. The grasshopper laughed and replied that there was plenty of time. "Why should I work in this fine weather?" he said. "Summer will last for many more days." The ant said nothing and continued its work. It stored wheat, rice and seeds in its safe store. Sometimes it stopped to rest in the shade, but it never forgot the coming winter. The grasshopper, on the other hand, sang from morning to evening. It believed that food would always be easy to find. One afternoon, the grasshopper asked the ant why it worked so hard when the sun was shining. The ant answered that summer food would not last forever, and a wise worker prepares for the season that is coming. The grasshopper only laughed and sang a louder song. It danced in the grass and told the ant to enjoy the summer while it lasted. Soon the warm days ended. Cold rain covered the fields, insects disappeared, and the grasshopper found nothing to eat. Hungry and shivering, it went to the ant's shelter and asked for help. The ant shared a small meal but explained that kindness could not replace planning. "I warned you in summer," it said gently. "You must gather food whenever spring returns and balance enjoyment with responsibility." The grasshopper understood that it had confused leisure with a life without duties. It thanked the ant and promised to change. When warm weather came again, it worked beside the ant each morning and sang only after storing enough food. The two friends remained helpful to one another, and the grasshopper never forgot the lesson of that cold winter. The ant smiled and welcomed its friend, because a good neighbour helps, but a good worker also remembers the lesson. Moral Prepare during good times, and do not sacrifice necessary work for immediate pleasure. Padma Bridge Paragraph in 150 Words Best for Class 6–7. The Padma Multipurpose Bridge is one of Bangladesh's most important transport projects. It crosses the broad Padma River and links Mawa in Munshiganj with Jajira in Shariatpur. In this way it gives the south-western districts a direct connection with Dhaka and the northern and eastern parts of the country. The bridge was inaugurated on 25 June 2022 and opened to road traffic the next day. It is about 6.15 kilometres long and has two levels: the upper deck carries a four-lane road, while the lower deck is designed for a single railway track. Forty-two piers support forty-one steel spans. The bridge has reduced dependence on ferries and made travel more predictable. Farmers can send products to markets more quickly, and people in the connected districts can reach hospitals, schools, and workplaces with greater ease. Trains began crossing the bridge in October 2023, and the project was financed from Bangladesh's own public resources. Padma Bridge Paragraph in 250 Words Best for Class 8–10 and SSC. Internet Paragraph in 150 Words Best for Class 6–7. The internet is a worldwide network that connects millions of computers, phones and other devices. It lets people share information, pictures and messages across great distances in a few seconds. Today it is used in homes, schools, offices, hospitals and banks all over the world. For students, the internet is a powerful tool for learning. A learner can search for explanations, read digital books, watch a lesson, submit homework or speak with a teacher. Families use it for communication, shopping, banking, work and entertainment. It also helps people learn new skills at any age. But the internet also has dangers. Not everything online is true or safe, so we should check reliable sources and protect our passwords. We should never share personal photos or information with strangers. Spending too much time online can damage sleep and study. Used with balance and good sense, the internet helps learning and brings people closer. Internet Paragraph in 250 Words Best for Class 8–10 and SSC. The internet is a worldwide network that connects millions of computers, phones and other devices. It lets people share information, pictures, videos and messages across great distances in a few seconds. In a short time it has become a part of daily life. It has changed the way we study, work, shop and talk to one another. Today it is used in homes, schools, offices, hospitals, banks and shops all over the world. For students, the internet is a powerful tool for learning. A learner can search for explanations, read digital books, watch a recorded lesson, submit homework, practise a language or speak with a teacher. It also helps people of any age learn new skills, find jobs and read news from around the world. During school closures, online classes helped millions of students continue their studies from home. Families use it for communication, shopping, banking, work and entertainment, and doctors can even advise patients from a distance. But the internet also has dangers that we must understand. Not everything online is true or safe, so we should check reliable sources before believing or sharing news. We should use strong passwords, keep our accounts private, and never share personal photos or information with strangers. Spending too much time online can damage sleep, health and study habits. Parents and teachers should guide young users, and young users should ask an adult when something online feels wrong or frightening. If we use it with balance, self-control and good sense, the internet becomes a great helper for learning and brings people closer together. Internet Paragraph in 300 Words Best for SSC and HSC. Spending too much time online can damage sleep, health and study habits, and it can reduce face-to-face conversation with family and friends. Parents and teachers should guide young users, and young users should ask an adult when something online feels wrong or frightening. If we use it with balance, self-control and good sense, the internet becomes a great helper for learning and brings people closer together. title: Our National Flag Paragraph for Class 6, 7, 8, SSC and HSC
excerpt: On this page you will find our national flag paragraph in 150, 250 and 300 words for Class 6 to 12, SSC and HSC. The short version is best for junior classes,
plainContent: On this page you will find our national flag paragraph in 150, 250 and 300 words for Class 6 to 12, SSC and HSC. The short version is best for junior classes, and the longer versions are best for SSC and HSC. A Bangla meaning, important word meanings and exam tips are given at the end. Our National Flag Paragraph in 150 Words Best for Class 6–7. A national flag is the sign of a country's identity and independence. Our national flag is a green rectangle with a red circle placed towards the hoist. The green field stands for the lush land of Bangladesh, its youth and vitality. The red circle stands for the rising sun over Bengal and the blood of the martyrs who died for our freedom. Our present flag was adopted on 17 January 1972. It was designed by the artist Quamrul Hassan. An earlier wartime flag carried a map of Bangladesh inside the red circle, but the map was later removed to make the flag simple and clear. The flag was first raised in an earlier form at Dhaka University on 2 March 1971. Today it flies on Independence Day, Victory Day, in schools and on government buildings. We should keep it clean, handle it with respect and never let it touch the ground. Our National Flag Paragraph in 250 Words Best for Class 8–10 and SSC. A national flag is the sign of a country's identity and independence. It is not only a piece of cloth; it carries the history, hopes and sacrifices of a nation. Our national flag is a green rectangle with a red circle placed slightly towards the hoist, so that the circle looks centred when the flag flies in the wind. The green field stands for the lush green land of Bangladesh, its youth and vitality. The red circle stands for the rising sun over Bengal and for the blood of the martyrs who died for our freedom. The flag has a short but proud history. An earlier version, with a map of Bangladesh inside the red circle, was first raised at Dhaka University on 2 March 1971, before the Liberation War began. After independence, the artist Quamrul Hassan refined the design and removed the map, because a map was hard to draw correctly on a small flag. The present flag was officially adopted on 17 January 1972. Its length and width follow the ratio of 10 to 6, and the red circle has a radius of one-fifth of the length. Today our flag flies on Independence Day and Victory Day, in schools, colleges and government offices, and at international events. It reminds us of the sacrifices of 1971 and of our duty to build a better country. Students should learn to handle the flag with care, keep it clean, and never let it touch the ground. Respect for the flag is respect for the people and history it represents. Our National Flag Paragraph in 300 Words Best for SSC and HSC. A national flag is the sign of a country's identity and independence. It is not only a piece of cloth; it carries the history, hopes and sacrifices of a nation. Our national flag is a green rectangle with a red circle placed slightly towards the hoist, so that the circle looks centred when the flag flies in the wind. The green field stands for the lush green land of Bangladesh, its youth and vitality. The red circle stands for the rising sun over Bengal and for the blood of the martyrs who died for our freedom in 1971. The flag has a short but proud history. An earlier version, with a golden map of Bangladesh inside the red circle, was designed by student leaders and first raised at Dhaka University on 2 March 1971, before the Liberation War began. After independence, the artist Quamrul Hassan refined the design and removed the map, because a map was hard to draw correctly on a small flag and looked different from each side. The present flag was officially adopted on 17 January 1972. Its length and width follow the ratio of 10 to 6, and the red circle has a radius of one-fifth of the length. Today our flag flies on Independence Day and Victory Day, in schools, colleges and government offices, and at international events where Bangladesh is represented. It reminds us of the sacrifices of 1971 and of our duty to build an honest and hardworking country. title: Importance of Female Education Paragraph

plainContent: On this page you will find importance of female education paragraph in 150, 250 and 300 words for Class 6 to 12, SSC and HSC. The short version is best for junior classes, and the longer versions are best for SSC and HSC. A Bangla meaning, important word meanings and exam tips are given at the end. Importance of Female Education Paragraph in 150 Words Best for Class 6–7. Female education means giving girls the same chance to learn as boys. Education is a basic right, not a favour. Girls need education for the same reasons boys do: learning builds knowledge, confidence, practical skills and the ability to make good decisions. An educated girl can care for her health and earn a living. An educated woman can understand her rights and help her family and country. She can teach her children, look after their health and send them to school. Keeping girls in school also helps future generations, because educated mothers value health and learning for their children. Yet many girls still leave school early. Poverty, unsafe travel, early marriage and old social ideas stand in their way. Families, schools and the government should work together to remove these problems. Supporting female education creates opportunity, reduces inequality and strengthens society. No country can develop while half of its people stay uneducated. Importance of Female Education Paragraph in 250 Words Best for Class 8–10 and SSC. Female education means giving girls the same chance to learn as boys. Education is a basic right, not a favour. Girls need education for the same reasons boys do: learning builds knowledge, confidence, practical skills and the ability to make good decisions. An educated girl can care for her health, earn a living and stand on her own feet. A girl who studies can choose her own future instead of depending on others for every decision. An educated woman can understand her rights and help her family and country. She can teach her children, look after their health and send them to school. Keeping girls in school also helps future generations, because educated mothers value health and learning for their children. Educated women also take better care of their children's food, vaccination and schooling. When women earn, the whole family becomes stronger, and the country gains skilled workers, teachers, doctors and leaders. Yet many girls still leave school early. Poverty, unsafe travel, early marriage and old social ideas stand in their way. Some families think a girl's place is only at home, and this idea harms both the girl and the nation. Families, schools and the government should work together to remove these problems. Safe transport, free books, scholarships and awareness campaigns can keep girls in school. Supporting female education creates opportunity, reduces inequality and strengthens society for all. No country can develop while half of its people stay uneducated. Importance of Female Education Paragraph in 300 Words Best for SSC and HSC. Female education means giving girls the same chance to learn as boys. Education is a basic right, not a favour. Girls need education for the same reasons boys do: learning builds knowledge, confidence, practical skills and the ability to make good decisions. An educated girl can care for her health, earn a living and stand on her own feet. A girl who studies can choose her own future instead of depending on others for every decision. In the past, many people believed girls did not need schooling, but that idea is changing as people see educated women succeed. An educated woman can understand her rights and help her family and country. She can teach her children, look after their health and send them to school. Keeping girls in school also helps future generations, because educated mothers value health and learning for their children. Educated women also take better care of their children's food, vaccination and schooling. When women earn, the whole family becomes stronger, and the country gains skilled workers, teachers, doctors and leaders. A nation that educates its daughters educates its future, because mothers are a child's first teacher. Yet many girls still leave school early. Poverty, unsafe travel, early marriage and old social ideas stand in their way. Some families think a girl's place is only at home, and this idea harms both the girl and the nation. Families, schools and the government should work together to remove these problems. Safe transport, free books, scholarships and awareness campaigns can keep girls in school. Supporting female education creates opportunity, reduces inequality and strengthens society for all. No country can develop while half of its people stay uneducated. Every girl deserves a classroom, a book and a dream, and society must give her all three. plainContent: On this page you will find environment pollution paragraph in 150, 250 and 300 words for Class 6 to 12, SSC and HSC. The short version is best for junior classes, and the longer versions are best for SSC and HSC. A Bangla meaning, important word meanings and exam tips are given at the end. Environment Pollution Paragraph in 150 Words Best for Class 6–7. The environment is everything around us: air, water, soil, plants and animals. Environment pollution means making our surroundings dirty and harmful. Air, water and soil become polluted when smoke, chemicals, sewage, plastic and other waste are released carelessly. A polluted environment harms people, animals and plants. Smoke from vehicles and factories pollutes the air, and people breathe it every day. Smoke also makes the sky grey and the air hard to breathe. Dirty water from homes and factories enters rivers and ponds. Plastic bags and bottles block drains and harm fish. Polluted surroundings can cause illness and make cities uncomfortable to live in. We can reduce pollution by planting trees, using bins, reducing plastic and saving water and electricity. Factories should use cleaner methods, and authorities must collect waste and treat sewage properly. Protecting the environment is a daily duty for everyone. Environment Pollution Paragraph in 250 Words Best for Class 8–10 and SSC. The environment is everything around us: air, water, soil, plants and animals. Environment pollution means making our surroundings dirty and harmful. Air, water and soil become polluted when smoke, chemicals, sewage, plastic and other waste are released carelessly. A polluted environment harms people, animals and plants, and it makes life harder for everyone. When the air is dirty, children and old people suffer most, because their bodies are weaker. Smoke from vehicles and factories pollutes the air, and people breathe it every day. Smoke also makes the sky grey and the air hard to breathe. Dirty water from homes and factories enters rivers and ponds, and fish die when the water becomes poisonous. Burning rubbish in the open adds smoke and bad smell to the air, and it can make breathing difficult. Plastic bags and bottles block drains and harm fish and birds. Polluted surroundings can cause illness, reduce soil fertility and make cities uncomfortable to live in. We can reduce pollution by planting trees, using bins, reducing plastic and saving water and electricity. Factories should use cleaner methods, and authorities must collect waste and treat sewage properly. Schools can teach children to keep their surroundings clean. Protecting the environment is not an occasional campaign; it is a daily duty for households, schools, businesses and government. Clean surroundings support healthy lives and a safer future for all of us. Every small action counts: a tree planted today gives shade, fruit and clean air for years. Environment Pollution Paragraph in 300 Words Best for SSC and HSC. The environment is everything around us: air, water, soil, plants and animals. Environment pollution means making our surroundings dirty and harmful. Air, water and soil become polluted when smoke, chemicals, sewage, plastic and other waste are released carelessly. A polluted environment harms people, animals and plants, and it makes life harder for everyone. When the air is dirty, children and old people suffer most, because their bodies are weaker. Trees clean the air, give us oxygen and keep the land cool, so cutting them down makes pollution worse. Smoke from vehicles and factories pollutes the air, and people breathe it every day. Smoke also makes the sky grey and the air hard to breathe. Dirty water from homes and factories enters rivers and ponds, and fish die when the water becomes poisonous. Burning rubbish in the open adds smoke and bad smell to the air, and it can make breathing difficult. Plastic bags and bottles block drains and harm fish and birds. Loud noise from horns and machines is also a kind of pollution, because it disturbs sleep and harms hearing. Polluted surroundings can cause illness, reduce soil fertility and make cities uncomfortable to live in. We can reduce pollution by planting trees, using bins, reducing plastic and saving water and electricity. Factories should use cleaner methods, and authorities must collect waste and treat sewage properly. Schools can teach children to keep their surroundings clean. Protecting the environment is not an occasional campaign; it is a daily duty for households, schools, businesses and government. Clean surroundings support healthy lives and a safer future for all of us. Every small action counts: a tree planted today gives shade, fruit and clean air for years. If we all act together, our country can become cleaner, healthier and more beautiful. Mobile Phone Paragraph in 150 Words Best for Class 6–7. A mobile phone is a portable device used for calls, messages, photography, internet access, navigation, learning and emergency help. Today almost every person carries one in a pocket. Students can use educational apps, dictionaries, recorded lessons and online libraries. Families can stay connected even when members live far apart. But a phone becomes harmful when it controls the user. Excessive gaming and social media can reduce sleep, attention, physical activity and face-to-face conversation. Many students check their phones hundreds of times a day without noticing it. Distracted driving, unsafe sharing of photos, scams and cyberbullying are other serious risks. We should keep phones away during study and meals, protect personal information and follow school and road rules. Parents should guide young users and set time limits. We should use the phone as a tool, not let the phone use us. A phone is useful equipment when guided by self-control. Mobile Phone Paragraph in 250 Words Best for Class 8–10 and SSC.
