title: Road Accident Paragraph
excerpt: On this page you will find road accident paragraph in 150, 250 and 300 words for Class 6 to 12, SSC and HSC. The short version is best for junior classes, and
plainContent: On this page you will find road accident paragraph in 150, 250 and 300 words for Class 6 to 12, SSC and HSC. The short version is best for junior classes, and the longer versions are best for SSC and HSC. A Bangla meaning, important word meanings and exam tips are given at the end. Road Accident Paragraph in 150 Words Best for Class 6–7. A road accident is a collision or other harmful incident involving vehicles, pedestrians, cyclists or roadside objects. It may happen on a highway, street, bridge or village road. Every day, road accidents take lives and injure people in our country. Speeding, reckless overtaking, driving while tired, using a phone and ignoring signals are common causes. Poor lighting, damaged roads, untrained drivers and careless pedestrians add to the danger. Accidents cause death, injury, disability, emotional pain and financial loss. A single crash can affect an entire family and delay traffic for thousands of people. No punishment after a crash can bring back a lost life. Safety begins with behaviour. Drivers should obey speed limits, wear seat belts or helmets, avoid alcohol and phones, and never drive when exhausted. Pedestrians should use footpaths and crossings and look carefully before crossing. Authorities must also enforce licensing rules, repair roads and improve signs and lighting. Road safety is a shared responsibility. Road Accident Paragraph in 250 Words Best for Class 8–10 and SSC. A road accident is a collision or other harmful incident involving vehicles, pedestrians, cyclists or roadside objects. It may happen on a highway, street, bridge or village road. Every day, road accidents take lives and injure people in our country. Most accidents do not happen by chance; they happen because someone breaks a rule. Speeding, reckless overtaking, driving while tired, using a phone and ignoring signals are common causes. Driving an unfit vehicle also causes many crashes. Poor lighting, damaged roads, untrained drivers and careless pedestrians add to the danger. Accidents cause death, injury, disability, emotional pain and financial loss. A single crash can affect an entire family and delay traffic for thousands of people. No punishment after a crash can bring back a lost life. Children crossing roads near schools are in special danger, so drivers must slow down there. A family that loses its earning member may fall into poverty for years. Safety begins with behaviour. Drivers should obey speed limits, wear seat belts or helmets, avoid alcohol and phones, and never drive when exhausted. Pedestrians should use footpaths and crossings and look carefully before crossing. Authorities must also enforce licensing rules, inspect vehicles, repair roads, improve signs and lighting, and educate the public. Emergency services should reach crash sites quickly. Schools and parents should teach children road rules from an early age. Road safety is a shared responsibility, and patience can save lives. A careful driver is a good citizen. Road Accident Paragraph in 300 Words Best for SSC and HSC. A road accident is a collision or other harmful incident involving vehicles, pedestrians, cyclists or roadside objects. It may happen on a highway, street, bridge or village road. Every day, road accidents take lives and injure people in our country. Driving an unfit vehicle also causes many crashes. A driver who respects the speed limit respects the lives of others. Poor lighting, damaged roads, untrained drivers and careless pedestrians add to the danger. Accidents cause death, injury, disability, emotional pain and financial loss. A single crash can affect an entire family and delay traffic for thousands of people. No punishment after a crash can bring back a lost life. Children crossing roads near schools are in special danger, so drivers must slow down there. A family that loses its earning member may fall into poverty for years. Prevention is always better than regret. After an accident, the injured need quick help, and bystanders should call for an ambulance at once. Safety begins with behaviour. Drivers should obey speed limits, wear seat belts or helmets, avoid alcohol and phones, and never drive when exhausted. Pedestrians should use footpaths and crossings and look carefully before crossing. Authorities must also enforce licensing rules, inspect vehicles, repair roads, improve signs and lighting, and educate the public. Emergency services should reach crash sites quickly. Schools and parents should teach children road rules from an early age. Road safety is a shared responsibility, and patience can save lives. A careful driver is a good citizen. If drivers, pedestrians and authorities each do their part, our roads can become much safer. title: Dialogue How to Make a Good Result
excerpt: This dialogue is about how to make a good result in the examination. It is written for Class 6 to 10, SSC and HSC students. The exam question is usually:
plainContent: This dialogue is about how to make a good result in the examination. It is written for Class 6 to 10, SSC and HSC students. The exam question is usually: "Write a dialogue between two friends about how to make a good result in the examination." Read the dialogue below, then learn the Bangla meaning and the important words at the end. The dialogue uses simple English, so you can learn it easily and rewrite it in your own words in the examination. Dialogue: How to Make a Good Result Kamal: Examinations are approaching, and I do not know how to organise my preparation. Jamal: Begin with a realistic timetable. List every subject, identify weak chapters, and assign short study periods with breaks. Kamal: I usually read the textbook repeatedly but forget it during the test. Jamal: Close the book and recall the main points. Solve practice questions, explain a lesson aloud, and review your mistakes rather than merely rereading. Kamal: Should I study all night before the examination? Jamal: No. Adequate sleep, nutritious food, exercise, and a calm mind improve memory. Keep your phone away during focused study and ask teachers about difficult topics. Kamal: I also lose marks because I rush through the question paper. Jamal: Practise writing within a time limit. In the examination, read the directions carefully, plan long answers, and leave a few minutes for checking. Kamal: My handwriting is slow, so I cannot finish long answers. Jamal: Then practise one long answer every day with a watch beside you. Speed improves only by writing, not by reading alone. Kamal: What should I do the day before the examination? Jamal: Revise short notes, not the whole book. Prepare your pen, admit card and water bottle, and go to bed early. Kamal: I feel very nervous in the examination hall. Jamal: Take a deep breath and begin with the question you know best. Confidence grows after the first answer. Kamal: Should I study in a group or alone? Jamal: Both have value. Group study helps when you discuss a difficult lesson, but silent study is better for memorising and writing practice. Kamal: I often forget what I studied last week. Jamal: That is why revision is important. Read a lesson, then revise it after one day, after one week, and again before the examination. Kamal: What about model tests? Are they useful? Jamal: Yes. A model test shows your weak points and teaches you to finish within the time limit. Take one every week in the last month before the examination. Kamal: I will start today and measure progress by completed tasks, not by hours spent at the desk. Jamal: That is a sensible approach. Consistent effort usually produces better results than last-minute pressure. Bangla Meaning of the Dialogue সংলাপটির বাংলা অর্থ পরীক্ষা এগিয়ে আসছে, কিন্তু কামাল জানে না কীভাবে প্রস্তুতি গোছাবে। জামাল বলে, প্রথমে বাস্তবসম্মত একটি রুটিন বানাতে হবে — সব বিষয়ের তালিকা করে দুর্বল অধ্যায়গুলো চিহ্নিত করতে হবে এবং ছোট ছোট সময়ে বিরতিসহ পড়তে হবে। শুধু বই বারবার পড়লে পরীক্ষার হলে মনে থাকে না। বই বন্ধ করে মূল বিষয়গুলো মনে করার চেষ্টা করতে হবে, অনুশীলনী প্রশ্ন সমাধান করতে হবে এবং ভুলগুলো ঝালিয়ে নিতে হবে। রাত জেগে পড়া উচিত নয় — পর্যাপ্ত ঘুম, পুষ্টিকর খাবার, ব্যায়াম ও শান্ত মন স্মৃতিশক্তি বাড়ায়। পরীক্ষার হলে তাড়াহুড়ো না করে প্রশ্ন ভালোভাবে পড়ে, লম্বা উত্তরের পরিকল্পনা করে এবং শেষে কিছু সময় রেখে উত্তর যাচাই করতে হবে। পরীক্ষার আগের দিন পুরো বই নয়, ছোট নোট ঝালিয়ে নিতে হবে। শেষে কামাল আজ থেকেই শুরু করার সিদ্ধান্ত নেয়। জামাল আরও বলে, দলগত পড়া কঠিন পাঠ আলোচনার জন্য ভালো, আর নীরবে পড়া মুখস্থ ও লেখার অনুশীলনের জন্য ভালো। একবার পড়ে ভুলে যাওয়া স্বাভাবিক, তাই একদিন পর, এক সপ্তাহ পর এবং পরীক্ষার আগে আবার ঝালিয়ে নিতে হবে। মডেল টেস্ট দুর্বল দিকগুলো দেখিয়ে দেয় এবং নির্ধারিত সময়ের মধ্যে শেষ করতে শেখায়। পরীক্ষার আগের মাসে প্রতি সপ্তাহে একটি মডেল টেস্ট দেওয়া উচিত। Important Word Meanings English Word Bangla Meaning Organise গোছানো Realistic বাস্তবসম্মত Identify চিহ্নিত করা Recall স্মরণ করা Adequate পর্যাপ্ত Nutritious পুষ্টিকর Consistent ধারাবাহিক, নিয়মিত Approach পদ্ধতি Nervous নার্ভাস, উদ্বিগ্ন Confidence আত্মবিশ্বাস Exam Tips Write the dialogue as a conversation, not as a paragraph. Put the speaker's name and a colon before each line. Keep the language simple and natural, the way two friends really talk about their examination worries. Give practical study advice in the dialogue — a timetable, recalling instead of rereading, practice writing, and checking answers — instead of only saying that hard work is good. Give the dialogue a clear ending, such as a decision to start preparation today. Learn the important words from the table so that you can write the dialogue in your own sentences in the exam. Do not try to learn everything on the last day. Revise short notes, prepare your pen and admit card, and sleep early the night before the examination. title: Advantage & Disadvantage of Village life and City life Dialogue
excerpt: This dialogue compares village life and city life — their advantages and disadvantages. It is written for Class 6 to 10, SSC and HSC students. The exam
plainContent: This dialogue compares village life and city life — their advantages and disadvantages. It is written for Class 6 to 10, SSC and HSC students. The exam question is usually: "Write a dialogue between two friends about the advantages and disadvantages of village life and city life." Read the dialogue below, then learn the Bangla meaning and the important words at the end. The dialogue uses simple English, so you can learn it easily and rewrite it in your own words in the examination. Dialogue: Village Life and City Life Rasel: Would you prefer to live in a village or a city? Mita: I enjoy village life because it is quieter, greener, and closer to fields and open water. Neighbours often know one another and help during difficulties. Rasel: Cities offer more colleges, hospitals, jobs, libraries, and cultural events. Public transport and internet services may also be easier to find. Mita: That is true, but cities can be crowded, noisy, polluted, and expensive. A small flat in the city costs more than a whole house in a village. Rasel: Villages also have problems. They may have limited specialist healthcare, employment, and reliable transport. Mita: I agree. A serious patient from a village often has to travel to the city for treatment. And many village students come to the city for higher education. Rasel: Rural areas are changing too. Better roads, schools, and digital connections can provide opportunities without destroying their peaceful character. Mita: And cities can learn from villages by protecting open spaces, reducing pollution, and encouraging community relationships. Rasel: Which life is better for children, in your opinion? Mita: Village children grow up close to nature and learn practical work early. City children get better schools and more activities, but they have little open space to play. Rasel: Food is another difference. Village food is often fresh from the field, while city food may be costly and less fresh. Mita: But the city offers variety — different foods, books, games, and jobs in one place. Rasel: What about the environment? Which place is cleaner? Mita: Villages are usually cleaner because there are fewer vehicles and factories. Cities suffer from smoke, dust and waste, though some cities are now planting trees and cleaning their rivers. Rasel: Jobs are also different. In a village, most people work in farming or fishing. In a city, people work in offices, factories, shops and services. Mita: That is true, but many village people now earn money from small businesses, handicrafts and online work. The internet has brought new jobs to the village too. Rasel: Neither way of life is perfect. The right choice depends on a person's work, family, and needs. Mita: Improving both places is more useful than arguing that one is always superior. Bangla Meaning of the Dialogue সংলাপটির বাংলা অর্থ রাসেল জানতে চায়, গ্রামের জীবন ভালো নাকি শহরের জীবন ভালো। মিতা বলে, গ্রামের জীবন শান্ত, সবুজ এবং মাঠ ও খোলা পানির কাছাকাছি। প্রতিবেশীরা একে অন্যকে চেনে এবং বিপদে সাহায্য করে। শহরে কলেজ, হাসপাতাল, চাকরি, লাইব্রেরি ও সাংস্কৃতিক অনুষ্ঠান বেশি। কিন্তু শহর ভিড়, শব্দ, দূষণ ও ব্যয়বহুল। গ্রামে বিশেষজ্ঞ চিকিৎসা, চাকরি ও নির্ভরযোগ্য যানবাহনের অভাব আছে। তবে গ্রামও বদলাচ্ছে — ভালো রাস্তা, স্কুল ও ইন্টারনেট সেখানে সুযোগ এনে দিচ্ছে। শহরও গ্রাম থেকে শিখতে পারে — খোলা জায়গা রক্ষা করা, দূষণ কমানো এবং প্রতিবেশীর সম্পর্ক বাড়ানো। কোনো জীবনই নিখুঁত নয়; কোনটি ভালো তা নির্ভর করে মানুষের কাজ, পরিবার ও প্রয়োজনের উপর। পরিবেশের দিক থেকেও দুই জীবনে পার্থক্য আছে। গ্রাম সাধারণত পরিচ্ছন্ন, কারণ সেখানে যানবাহন ও কারখানা কম। শহরে ধোঁয়া, ধুলো ও বর্জ্যের সমস্যা বেশি, যদিও কিছু শহর এখন গাছ লাগাচ্ছে ও নদী পরিষ্কার করছে। গ্রামে বেশিরভাগ মানুষ কৃষি ও মৎস্য কাজে যুক্ত, আর শহরে অফিস, কারখানা, দোকান ও সেবার কাজ বেশি। তবে ইন্টারনেটের কারণে গ্রামেও এখন ছোট ব্যবসা, হস্তশিল্প ও অনলাইন কাজের সুযোগ তৈরি হয়েছে। Important Word Meanings English Word Bangla Meaning Prefer পছন্দ করা Advantage সুবিধা Disadvantage অসুবিধা Crowded জনাকীর্ণ, ভিড়ে ভরা Polluted দূষিত Expensive ব্যয়বহুল Reliable নির্ভরযোগ্য Community সমাজ, প্রতিবেশী সমাজ Superior উত্তম, শ্রেষ্ঠ Variety বৈচিত্র্য Exam Tips Write the dialogue as a conversation, not as a paragraph. Put the speaker's name and a colon before each line. Keep the language simple and natural, the way two friends really discuss where they would like to live. Give points for both sides — the peace and fresh food of village life, and the schools, hospitals and jobs of city life — and also mention the problems of each. End with a balanced conclusion instead of saying that one place is always better than the other. Words like advantage, disadvantage, crowded and reliable will help you express both sides clearly. title: Discipline Composition
excerpt: On this page you will find a discipline composition with an outline, the full composition, a Bangla meaning, important word meanings and exam tips. It is
plainContent: On this page you will find a discipline composition with an outline, the full composition, a Bangla meaning, important word meanings and exam tips. It is written in simple English for Class 6 to 10, SSC and HSC students, so you can learn the main points easily and write the composition in your own words in the examination hall. Outline What discipline is: following rules and doing duties on time Discipline in the daily life of a student Discipline at home, at school, at work and in public life Life without discipline: talent wasted How to build discipline step by step: small habits and a realistic daily routine Conclusion: discipline is the key to success Discipline Composition Discipline means following good rules and doing our duties at the proper time. It does not mean fear or punishment; it means controlling ourselves so that a small comfort today does not destroy a big goal tomorrow. A disciplined person wakes up on time, keeps his things in order, finishes his work on time, and respects the rules of his family, school and society. Discipline is not a burden. It is a habit that makes life orderly, peaceful and successful. Just as a train cannot run without rails, a person cannot reach his goal without discipline. Discipline is most important in the life of a student. A disciplined student attends classes regularly, listens to his teachers, studies every day, and submits his homework on time. He keeps his books and notes tidy, prepares his lessons before class, and never copies in the examination. He respects his teachers and classmates, speaks politely, and follows the rules of his school. Such a student earns the love of his teachers and the trust of his friends, and he moves steadily towards success. Discipline is also needed outside school. At home, it means helping parents, keeping things in their place, and eating and sleeping on time. At work, it means arriving on time and finishing duties with care. In public life, it means obeying traffic rules, standing in a queue, keeping the roads and parks clean, and keeping promises. Discipline also teaches us to respect the rights of others. When people follow such rules, society becomes peaceful and safe. A country cannot progress if its people do not follow discipline. Without discipline, even talent is wasted. A clever student may fail because he studies only at the last moment. A strong player may lose because he does not practise regularly. Discipline turns small daily efforts into great skill, and it builds self-respect, because a person learns that he can depend on his own decisions. But discipline should be realistic: we must keep time for sleep, play, family and rest, or it will become a burden. With patience and daily practice, discipline becomes a habit, and that habit is the key to success in life. Let us practise discipline every day, from small things, and build a better future. Bangla Meaning শৃঙ্খলার বাংলা অর্থ শৃঙ্খলা মানে ভালো নিয়ম মেনে চলা এবং সময়মতো নিজের কর্তব্য পালন করা। শৃঙ্খলা মানে ভয় বা শাস্তি নয়; এর মানে নিজেকে নিয়ন্ত্রণ করা, যাতে আজকের ছোট আরাম আগামী দিনের বড় লক্ষ্য নষ্ট না করে। শৃঙ্খলাপরায়ণ মানুষ সময়মতো ঘুম থেকে ওঠে, জিনিসপত্র গুছিয়ে রাখে, সময়মতো কাজ শেষ করে এবং পরিবার, স্কুল ও সমাজের নিয়ম মেনে চলে। ছাত্রজীবনে শৃঙ্খলা সবচেয়ে বেশি দরকার। শৃঙ্খলাপরায়ণ ছাত্র নিয়মিত ক্লাসে যায়, প্রতিদিন পড়ে, সময়মতো বাড়ির কাজ জমা দেয় এবং পরীক্ষায় কখনো নকল করে না। বাড়িতে, কর্মক্ষেত্রে ও জনজীবনেও শৃঙ্খলা দরকার—যেমন ট্রাফিক নিয়ম মানা, লাইনে দাঁড়ানো, রাস্তা পরিষ্কার রাখা ও কথা রাখা। শৃঙ্খলা ছাড়া প্রতিভাও নষ্ট হয়ে যায়। ছোট ছোট প্রতিদিনের চেষ্টাই শৃঙ্খলার মাধ্যমে বড় দক্ষতায় পরিণত হয়। তবে শৃঙ্খলা হতে হবে বাস্তবসম্মত—ঘুম, খেলা, পরিবার ও বিশ্রামের জন্যও সময় রাখতে হবে। ধৈর্য ও নিয়মিত অভ্যাসে শৃঙ্খলা জীবনের সাফল্যের চাবিকাঠি হয়ে ওঠে। প্রতিদিন ছোট ছোট নিয়ম মেনে চললেই শৃঙ্খলা অভ্যাসে পরিণত হয়। Important Word Meanings English Word Bangla Meaning Discipline শৃঙ্খলা Duty কর্তব্য Control নিয়ন্ত্রণ Punctual সময়নিষ্ঠ Polite ভদ্র Queue সারি Obey মান্য করা Talent প্রতিভা Realistic বাস্তবসম্মত Patience ধৈর্য Exam Tips Learn the outline first — what discipline is, student life, home and public life, life without it — then write the composition in your own words in the examination hall. Do not memorise the whole composition. Remember the main points and write them in your own simple, correct sentences. Use short paragraphs: one for the meaning of discipline, one for student life, one for public life, and one short paragraph for the conclusion. Keep your spelling, grammar and handwriting neat and correct. A few correct sentences are better than many wrong ones. Revise the composition once again the night before the exam and read the Bangla meaning to remember the ideas clearly. title: Student life Composition for Class 5, 6, 7, 8, SSC – Easy

plainContent: On this page you will find a student life composition with an outline, the full composition, a Bangla meaning, important word meanings and exam tips. It is written in simple English for Class 5 to 10 and SSC students, so you can learn the main points easily and write the composition in your own words in the examination hall. Outline What student life is and why it is the best time of life The first duty of a student: sincere study and good habits Character, discipline and respect for teachers and parents Games, sports, health and co-curricular activities Problems of student life and how to face them Conclusion: good habits in student life build a bright and happy future Student Life Composition Student life is the best period of a person's life. It is the time to learn, to build character, and to prepare for the future. A student does not study only to pass examinations; he studies to gain knowledge, to form good habits, and to become a useful citizen. The lessons and habits we learn in student life stay with us for our whole life. That is why student life is often called the seed time of life, because the seeds we sow now will grow into the fruits of our future. The first duty of a student is sincere study. He should attend classes regularly, listen to his teachers carefully, and ask questions when he does not understand a lesson. He should study every day, finish his homework on time, and revise his lessons before they are forgotten. A good student keeps his books and notes tidy, reads books outside his textbooks, and tries to understand his lessons instead of memorising them without meaning. He should also learn from his mistakes and never copy in an examination. Regular study, not study at the last moment, brings real success. Student life is not only about books. A student should also build a good character. He should respect his parents and teachers, love his classmates, speak the truth, and keep his promises. He should be disciplined and punctual, and he should take part in games, sports and cultural activities. Games keep the body healthy and the mind fresh, and they teach teamwork and fair play. A student may also join social work, which teaches kindness and responsibility towards others. Student life also has problems. Many students feel pressure about examinations, and some waste their time on the phone or in bad company. A student should face these problems with courage. He should keep a daily routine, sleep well, eat healthy food, and ask his teachers or parents for help when he faces a difficulty. If a student uses his time well, studies with sincerity, and keeps a good character, he can build a bright future for himself and for his country. In short, student life is the golden time of life, and we should use it wisely. title: Value of Time Composition for Class 6,7,8,SSC,HSC
excerpt: On this page you will find a value of time composition with an outline, the full composition, a Bangla meaning, important word meanings and exam tips. It is
plainContent: On this page you will find a value of time composition with an outline, the full composition, a Bangla meaning, important word meanings and exam tips. It is written in simple English for Class 6 to 10, SSC and HSC students, so you can learn the main points and write the composition in your own words in the examination hall. Outline What time is and why it cannot be bought back How wise people use time: planning, a daily routine and clear priorities How time is wasted: laziness, delay and useless habits The results of using time well and wasting it Why students must learn the value of time early Conclusion: time is life, so use every moment well Value of Time Composition Time is the most valuable thing in our life. We can earn money again if we lose it, and we can recover our health with care and treatment, but a moment that has passed can never come back. Time moves forward all the time, and it waits for nobody. That is why wise people say that time is more precious than gold. Every person gets the same twenty-four hours in a day, but some use those hours well and rise in life, while others waste them and fall behind. A wise person uses time with a plan. He fixes his daily work, gives study, rest, play and family their proper time, and begins his work on time. A student should make a daily routine, study every subject a little every day, and finish his homework before the last moment. When a big task comes, he should divide it into small parts and finish one part each day. In this way, no work becomes too heavy, and the mind stays free from worry. Punctuality is also a part of using time well, because a punctual person earns the trust of others. On the other hand, many people waste time without knowing it. They sit idle, keep putting off their work for tomorrow, and spend hours on useless chatting and scrolling on the phone. This habit is called procrastination, and it is the greatest enemy of success. When work is left for the last moment, it becomes a burden, and the result is poor. A student who wastes his time in class and at home cannot do well in the examination, however clever he may be. Lost time brings regret, but regret cannot bring back the lost hours. So we should value time from today. We should set small goals, keep a routine, and do our daily work in time. We should also keep time for rest and play, because a tired mind cannot work well. A person who uses his time well can learn more, do more, and live a happier life. Let us remember that time is life itself. If we waste time, we waste our life. If we use time well, we can build a bright future for ourselves and for our country. Bangla Meaning সময়ের মূল্যের বাংলা অর্থ সময় আমাদের জীবনের সবচেয়ে মূল্যবান সম্পদ। হারানো টাকা আবার আয় করা যায়, অসুস্থ শরীর যত্নে ভালো হতে পারে, কিন্তু যে মুহূর্ত একবার চলে যায় তা আর কখনো ফিরে আসে না। সময় কারো জন্য অপেক্ষা করে না। তাই জ্ঞানী মানুষ সময়কে সোনার চেয়েও দামি মনে করেন। বুদ্ধিমান মানুষ পরিকল্পনা করে সময় ব্যবহার করেন। তিনি প্রতিদিনের কাজের একটি রুটিন তৈরি করেন, পড়াশোনা, বিশ্রাম, খেলা ও পরিবারকে সঠিক সময় দেন এবং কাজ সময়মতো শুরু করেন। বড় কাজকে ছোট ছোট ভাগে ভাগ করে প্রতিদিন একটু একটু করে শেষ করলে কোনো কাজই ভারী মনে হয় না। অন্যদিকে অনেকে অলসতা ও কাজ ফেলে রাখার অভ্যাসে সময় নষ্ট করে। এতে কাজ জমে যায়, মন চিন্তায় ভরে যায় এবং পরীক্ষায় ফল খারাপ হয়। তাই আমাদের আজ থেকেই সময়ের মূল্য বুঝতে হবে। সময়মতো কাজ করলে আমরা বেশি শিখতে পারব, বেশি কাজ করতে পারব এবং উজ্জ্বল ভবিষ্যৎ গড়তে পারব। Important Word Meanings English Word Bangla Meaning Valuable মূল্যবান Precious অমূল্য Recover সুস্থ হওয়া Punctual সময়নিষ্ঠ Procrastination গড়িমসি Idle অলস Routine দৈনন্দিন রুটিন Burden বোঝা Regret অনুতাপ Trust আস্থা Exam Tips Learn the outline first — what time is, how to use it, how it is wasted, and the conclusion — then write the composition in your own words in the examination hall. title: Dengue Fever paragraph for Class 6,7,8, SSC, HSC
excerpt: On this page you will find dengue fever paragraph in 150, 250 and 300 words for Class 6 to 12, SSC and HSC. The short version is best for junior classes, and
plainContent: On this page you will find dengue fever paragraph in 150, 250 and 300 words for Class 6 to 12, SSC and HSC. The short version is best for junior classes, and the longer versions are best for SSC and HSC. A Bangla meaning, important word meanings and exam tips are given at the end. Dengue Fever Paragraph in 150 Words Best for Class 6–7. Dengue is a viral illness spread by the bite of infected Aedes mosquitoes. These mosquitoes breed in small amounts of clean standing water in buckets, flowerpots, tyres, roof gutters and uncovered tanks. They bite mainly during the day, especially in the early morning and late afternoon. A patient may develop sudden high fever, severe headache, pain behind the eyes, muscle and joint pain, nausea or a rash. Symptoms usually begin 4 to 10 days after the bite and last for 2 to 7 days. Most people recover in 1 to 2 weeks, but some develop severe dengue and need hospital care. Warning signs of severe dengue include severe stomach pain, repeated vomiting, bleeding gums, rapid breathing, tiredness and restlessness. Anyone with these signs should go to a hospital at once. Families can reduce risk by emptying containers, covering stored water and using mosquito nets. Community action is the strongest defence against dengue. Dengue Fever Paragraph in 250 Words Best for Class 8–10 and SSC. Dengue is a viral illness spread by the bite of infected Aedes mosquitoes. These mosquitoes breed in small amounts of clean standing water in buckets, flowerpots, tyres, roof gutters and uncovered tanks. They bite mainly during the day, especially in the early morning and late afternoon. Unlike many mosquitoes, the Aedes mosquito often lives near human homes, so the danger is close to us. It does not spread from person to person by touch. A patient may develop sudden high fever, severe headache, pain behind the eyes, muscle and joint pain, nausea or a rash. Symptoms usually begin 4 to 10 days after the bite and last for 2 to 7 days. Most people recover in 1 to 2 weeks, but some develop severe dengue and need hospital care. People infected for a second time, as well as young children, pregnant women and old people, face a greater risk of severe dengue. Warning signs of severe dengue often appear around 3 to 7 days after the illness begins, sometimes just as the fever falls. They include severe stomach pain, repeated vomiting, bleeding gums, rapid breathing, tiredness and restlessness. Anyone with these signs should go to a hospital at once. A patient should rest, drink plenty of liquids and take paracetamol for pain, but should avoid aspirin and ibuprofen, which increase the risk of bleeding. Families can reduce risk by emptying containers, covering stored water and using mosquito nets. Community action is the strongest defence against dengue. Dengue Fever Paragraph in 300 Words Best for SSC and HSC. Dengue is a viral illness spread by the bite of infected Aedes mosquitoes. These mosquitoes breed in small amounts of clean standing water in buckets, flowerpots, tyres, roof gutters and uncovered tanks. They bite mainly during the day, especially in the early morning and late afternoon. Unlike many mosquitoes, the Aedes mosquito often lives near human homes, so the danger is close to us. It does not spread from person to person by touch. The rainy season is the most dangerous time, because rain fills the containers where mosquitoes breed. A patient may develop sudden high fever, severe headache, pain behind the eyes, muscle and joint pain, nausea or a rash. Symptoms usually begin 4 to 10 days after the bite and last for 2 to 7 days. Most people recover in 1 to 2 weeks, but some develop severe dengue and need hospital care. People infected for a second time, as well as young children, pregnant women and old people, face a greater risk of severe dengue. High fever may reach 40 degrees Celsius, so the illness is sometimes called break-bone fever for the severe body pain it causes. Warning signs of severe dengue often appear around 3 to 7 days after the illness begins, sometimes just as the fever falls. They include severe stomach pain, repeated vomiting, bleeding gums, rapid breathing, tiredness and restlessness. Anyone with these signs should go to a hospital at once. A patient should rest, drink plenty of liquids and take paracetamol for pain, but should avoid aspirin and ibuprofen, which increase the risk of bleeding. Families can reduce risk by emptying containers, covering stored water and using mosquito nets. Community action is the strongest defence against dengue. Schools and local authorities should keep public areas clean, remove standing water and spread correct information. plainContent: On this page you will find a newspaper composition with an outline, the full composition, a Bangla meaning, important word meanings and exam tips. It is written in simple English for Class 6 to 10, SSC and HSC students, so you can learn the main points easily and write the composition in your own words in the examination hall. Outline What a newspaper is: printed and digital What we find inside a newspaper every day How a newspaper helps students How a newspaper helps society How to read a newspaper wisely and carefully Conclusion: a daily habit for an informed life Newspaper Composition A newspaper is a publication that comes out every day and tells us what is happening in our country and in the world. It may be printed on paper, or we may read it on a website or in an app on a mobile phone. Many newspapers are now published in both Bangla and English. A newspaper has many parts: national news, international news, education, science, health, business, sports, culture, weather, and advertisements. It also has editorials, letters from readers, and articles that explain important matters. In short, a newspaper is a storehouse of daily knowledge. A newspaper is very useful for students. A student who reads a newspaper every day learns many new words and improves his English. He learns about his country, the world, science, and sports, and he gets new ideas for essays, paragraphs and discussions. Reading the newspaper also helps him in examinations, because many questions in general knowledge and current affairs come from daily news. A student should read the newspaper for at least twenty minutes every day and note down new words and important facts in a notebook. A newspaper also helps society. It informs people about the decisions of the government, so they can understand their rights and duties. It exposes wrongdoing and corruption, and it speaks for people whose voices are not heard. It spreads new ideas about health, education, farming and technology, and it encourages people to think about problems and find solutions. It also publishes job advertisements, examination notices and useful information for students and job seekers. In this way, a newspaper builds public opinion and helps a country move forward on the right path. But a newspaper must be read with care. Not everything printed is true, and some news may be one-sided or incomplete. A wise reader checks the source, looks at the date, and compares the same news in more than one paper before believing it. News and opinion should not be confused: an editorial is the opinion of the paper, not a fact. We should also avoid spending all our time on sensational news. If we read a good newspaper every day with an open and careful mind, it will make us informed, thoughtful and responsible citizens. Bangla Meaning সংবাদপত্রের বাংলা অর্থ সংবাদপত্র এমন একটি প্রকাশনা যা প্রতিদিন প্রকাশিত হয় এবং দেশ-বিদেশের ঘটনা আমাদের জানায়। এটি কাগজে ছাপা হতে পারে, আবার মোবাইল ফোনে ওয়েবসাইট বা অ্যাপেও পড়া যায়। সংবাদপত্রে থাকে জাতীয় ও আন্তর্জাতিক সংবাদ, শিক্ষা, বিজ্ঞান, স্বাস্থ্য, ব্যবসা, খেলাধুলা, সংস্কৃতি, আবহাওয়া ও বিজ্ঞাপন। এতে সম্পাদকীয় ও পাঠকের চিঠিও থাকে। সংবাদপত্র ছাত্রদের জন্য খুবই উপকারী। প্রতিদিন সংবাদপত্র পড়লে ছাত্র নতুন শব্দ শেখে, ইংরেজি ভালো হয় এবং দেশ-বিদেশ সম্পর্কে জ্ঞান বাড়ে। রচনা, অনুচ্ছেদ ও আলোচনার জন্য নতুন ভাবনা পাওয়া যায়। সাধারণ জ্ঞান ও সাম্প্রতিক বিষয়ের অনেক প্রশ্ন দৈনিক সংবাদ থেকেই আসে। তাই প্রতিদিন অন্তত বিশ মিনিট সংবাদপত্র পড়া উচিত। সংবাদপত্র সমাজেরও উপকার করে। এটি সরকারের সিদ্ধান্ত জানায়, দুর্নীতি প্রকাশ করে এবং মানুষের অধিকার ও কর্তব্য বুঝতে সাহায্য করে। তবে সংবাদপত্র পড়তে হবে সতর্কভাবে—উৎস যাচাই করে, তারিখ দেখে এবং সংবাদ ও মতামতের পার্থক্য বুঝে। সংবাদপত্র পড়া একটি ভালো অভ্যাস, যা আমাদের জ্ঞান ও ভাষার দক্ষতা বাড়ায়। প্রতিদিন ভালো সংবাদপত্র পড়লে আমরা সচেতন ও দায়িত্বশীল নাগরিক হতে পারি। Important Word Meanings English Word Bangla Meaning Publication প্রকাশনা Editorial সম্পাদকীয় Advertisement বিজ্ঞাপন Current affairs সাম্প্রতিক বিষয় Corruption দুর্নীতি Expose প্রকাশ করা Opinion মতামত Sensational চাঞ্চল্যকর Informed অবহিত Citizen নাগরিক Exam Tips Learn the outline first — what a newspaper is, its parts, help for students, help for society, careful reading — then write the composition in your own words in the examination hall. title: Aim in Life Composition
excerpt: On this page you will find an aim in life composition with an outline, the full composition, a Bangla meaning, important word meanings and exam tips. It is
plainContent: On this page you will find an aim in life composition with an outline, the full composition, a Bangla meaning, important word meanings and exam tips. It is written in simple English for Class 6 to 10, SSC and HSC students, so you can learn the main points and write the composition in your own words in the examination hall. Outline What an aim in life is and why everyone needs one My aim: to become a teacher Why I have chosen this aim How I will prepare myself for it What I will do after reaching my aim Conclusion: an aim gives life a direction Aim in Life Composition An aim in life is a clear idea about what a person wants to become and what kind of work he wants to do. Every person should have an aim, because without an aim, life is like a boat without a rudder: it drifts in any direction and reaches nowhere. A person with an aim knows what to study, how to use his time, and how to face difficulties. An aim gives life a direction, and it gives a person the courage to work hard every day. My aim in life is to become a teacher. I have chosen this aim because education changes lives. A good teacher can open the minds of students, explain difficult lessons in simple words, and encourage shy learners to speak and ask questions. In our villages, many children still do not get good teaching, and I want to work for them. A teacher does not earn as much money as a doctor or an engineer, but the respect and love a teacher receives from students is a great reward. I want to become a teacher who makes learning easy and joyful for every child. To reach my aim, I must prepare myself from now. I must study regularly, read books outside my textbooks, and improve my English and Bangla. I must learn to speak clearly, to explain ideas in simple words, and to listen patiently to others. I must also build a good character, because a teacher must be honest, kind and disciplined. I will take advice from my teachers, learn from their methods, and practise teaching my younger brothers and sisters at home. Step by step, I will make myself ready for this noble profession. After becoming a teacher, I will serve my students with sincerity. I will try to make my lessons interesting, help weak students with extra care, and never behave rudely with anyone. I will also encourage my students to love their country, to respect their parents, and to help others. An aim is not only for personal success; it is also for serving society. If I can become a good teacher, I will feel that my life has a true meaning. That is why I will work hard every day to reach my aim in life. Bangla Meaning জীবনের লক্ষ্যের বাংলা অর্থ জীবনের লক্ষ্য মানে একজন মানুষ কী হতে চায় এবং কী ধরনের কাজ করতে চায় সে সম্পর্কে স্পষ্ট ধারণা। লক্ষ্য ছাড়া জীবন হাল ছাড়া নৌকার মতো—তা যেকোনো দিকে ভেসে যায়, কিন্তু কোথাও পৌঁছায় না। লক্ষ্য থাকলে মানুষ জানে কী পড়তে হবে, সময় কীভাবে ব্যবহার করতে হবে এবং কঠিন পরিস্থিতির মুখোমুখি কীভাবে হতে হবে। আমার জীবনের লক্ষ্য শিক্ষক হওয়া। আমি এই লক্ষ্য বেছে নিয়েছি, কারণ শিক্ষা মানুষের জীবন বদলে দেয়। একজন ভালো শিক্ষক ছাত্রদের মন খুলে দিতে পারেন, কঠিন পাঠ সহজ ভাষায় বোঝাতে পারেন এবং লাজুক ছাত্রদের প্রশ্ন করতে উৎসাহ দিতে পারেন। আমাদের গ্রামে অনেক শিশু এখনো ভালো শিক্ষা পায় না; আমি তাদের জন্য কাজ করতে চাই। শিক্ষকের বেতন ডাক্তার বা প্রকৌশলীর মতো বেশি না হলেও ছাত্রদের ভালোবাসা ও সম্মানই বড় পুরস্কার। লক্ষ্যে পৌঁছাতে আমাকে এখন থেকেই প্রস্তুতি নিতে হবে। নিয়মিত পড়াশোনা করতে হবে, পাঠ্যবইয়ের বাইরে বই পড়তে হবে এবং স্পষ্টভাবে কথা বলা ও ধৈর্য ধরে শোনা শিখতে হবে। শিক্ষক হয়ে আমি ছাত্রদের আন্তরিকভাবে সেবা করব, দুর্বল ছাত্রদের বাড়তি যত্ন নেব এবং তাদের দেশকে ভালোবাসতে শেখাব। লক্ষ্য শুধু নিজের সাফল্যের জন্য নয়, সমাজের সেবার জন্যও। Important Word Meanings English Word Bangla Meaning Aim লক্ষ্য Rudder হাল Direction দিকনির্দেশনা Encourage উৎসাহ দেওয়া Shy লাজুক Reward পুরস্কার Sincerity আন্তরিকতা Noble মহৎ Profession পেশা Patient ধৈর্যশীল Exam Tips Learn the outline first — what an aim is, my aim, why I chose it, how I will prepare — then write the composition in your own words. Do not memorise the whole composition. Remember the main points and write them in simple, correct sentences. Use short paragraphs: one for the meaning of an aim, one for why you chose it, one for preparation, and one for the conclusion. Keep your spelling and grammar correct. A few correct sentences are better than many wrong ones. Revise the composition once the night before the exam and read the Bangla meaning to remember the ideas clearly. title: The Pied Piper of Hamelin Completing Story
excerpt: This is the completing story of the Pied Piper of Hamelin, written for Class 6 to 10, SSC and HSC students. The given beginning is: "Long ago, the town of
plainContent: This is the completing story of the Pied Piper of Hamelin, written for Class 6 to 10, SSC and HSC students. The given beginning is: "Long ago, the town of Hamelin was full of rats. They entered houses, spoiled food, and frightened the people." Read the complete story below, then learn the moral, the Bangla meaning and the important words at the end. The story teaches us that a promise must be kept. The Pied Piper of Hamelin (Complete Story) Long ago, the town of Hamelin was full of rats. They entered houses, spoiled food, and frightened the people. The rats were so many that the people could not eat or sleep in peace. They chewed clothes, bit babies in their cradles, and ran through the streets day and night. The people went to the mayor and asked him to save the town. The mayor promised a large reward to anyone who could rid the town of the pests. Many people tried, but no one succeeded. Some set traps, some used poison, and some kept cats in their houses, but the rats were too many and too clever. Then a travelling piper arrived at the town gate. He wore a bright coat and carried a long pipe. He said that his music could lead the rats away. The mayor agreed to pay him a thousand gold coins if he could free the town. The piper stood in the market place and played a strange, bright tune. At once, every rat in the town came out of its hiding place. The rats followed the piper through the streets and out to the river. He guided them safely away, and the town was free at last. The piper returned to claim the promised payment. But the mayor had expected the piper to work for less, so he refused to pay the full reward. He offered only a small sum and told the piper to be glad of it. The piper warned him that a promise made publicly must be honoured, but the mayor dismissed him with laughter. The piper left the town hall quietly and stood in the street. Then he played another tune. This time the tune was sweet and sad, and every child in Hamelin followed him beyond the gates. When the mayor and the citizens realised what was happening, they ran after the piper and begged him to return the children. The piper stopped and said that he would bring them back only after the town paid what it had promised and apologised for breaking its word. The mayor agreed at once. The piper played his pipe again, and the children came back to their homes. From then on, the leaders of Hamelin kept their promises. Moral A promise is a responsibility, not an opportunity for dishonest bargaining. Bangla Meaning of the Story গল্পটির বাংলা অর্থ বহু আগে হ্যামেলিন শহর ইঁদুরে ভরে গিয়েছিল। ইঁদুরগুলো ঘরে ঢুকে খাবার নষ্ট করত এবং মানুষকে ভয় দেখাত। মেয়র ঘোষণা করলেন, যে শহরকে ইঁদুরমুক্ত করতে পারবে তাকে বড় পুরস্কার দেওয়া হবে। একদিন এক ভ্রমণকারী বংশীবাদক এলো। সে তার বাঁশির সুরে সব ইঁদুরকে শহরের বাইরে নদীর দিকে নিয়ে গেল। কিন্তু কাজ শেষ হলে মেয়র পুরো পুরস্কার দিতে অস্বীকার করলেন। তখন বংশীবাদক আবার বাঁশি বাজাল, আর এবার শহরের সব শিশু তার পিছু পিছু চলে গেল। মেয়র ও নগরবাসী ক্ষমা চেয়ে প্রতিশ্রুত পুরস্কার দিলে বংশীবাদক শিশুদের ফিরিয়ে আনল। এরপর থেকে হ্যামেলিনের নেতারা প্রতিশ্রুতি রক্ষা করতেন। অনেকেই চেষ্টা করেছিল — কেউ ফাঁদ পেতেছিল, কেউ বিষ ব্যবহার করেছিল, আবার কেউ বাড়িতে বিড়াল পুষেছিল। কিন্তু ইঁদুরের সংখ্যা এত বেশি ছিল যে কিছুই কাজ করল না। তখনই বংশীবাদক এসে তার সুরের জাদুতে সব ইঁদুরকে নদীর দিকে নিয়ে গেল। মেয়রের প্রতিশ্রুতি ভঙ্গের পরিণাম শহরবাসীকে শিখিয়েছিল, কথা রাখা কতটা জরুরি। Important Word Meanings English Word Bangla Meaning Mayor মেয়র Reward পুরস্কার Piper বংশীবাদক Tune সুর Honour সম্মান করা, রক্ষা করা Promise প্রতিশ্রুতি Dishonest অসৎ Bargaining দর কষাকষি Apologise ক্ষমা চাওয়া Citizen নাগরিক Exam Tips Begin the story with the given beginning exactly as it is written in the question, then continue it in your own words. Keep the events in order: the rats trouble the town, the piper leads them away, the mayor breaks his promise, the piper leads the children away, and the town pays and apologises. Write in the past tense, because the story happened in the past. Do not change the main idea of the story. The mayor must break his promise first, and the piper must bring the children back only after the promise is kept. End the story with the moral in a separate short paragraph, as shown above. Do not add a year or other details you are not sure about. The story is a legend, so "long ago" is enough. title: Application for Transfer Certificate
excerpt: On this page you will find an application for a transfer certificate for Class 6 to 12, SSC and HSC students. It explains when you need this certificate, shows
plainContent: On this page you will find an application for a transfer certificate for Class 6 to 12, SSC and HSC students. It explains when you need this certificate, shows the correct format, and gives a complete example that you can follow in your examination. A Bangla meaning, important word meanings and exam tips are given at the end. Format of an Application for a Transfer Certificate A transfer certificate application follows the usual format of a formal application to the headmaster or principal. Each part has a fixed place, so learn the order first and then practise writing the full application. The main parts are given below. Date Name and designation of the headmaster or principal Name and address of the school Subject of the application Salutation, such as "Sir" Body of the application Closing, such as "Yours obediently" Name, class and roll number of the student A transfer certificate is an official paper from your old school. It proves that you were a student there and that you have cleared your dues. A new school asks for it before it admits you, so write the application in clear and polite language and mention your class and roll number correctly. Application for a Transfer Certificate (Example) 10 June 2026 The Headmaster Rangpur Zilla School Rangpur Subject: Request for a transfer certificate Sir, I respectfully state that I am a student of Class Ten in your school. My family will move to another district because my father has been transferred there, and I must continue my studies in a new school. The new school has asked me to submit a transfer certificate before it completes my admission. I have paid all my school dues and returned the books I borrowed from the library. I have also tried to follow the rules of the school and attend my classes regularly. My teachers know me well, and I have always tried to behave politely with my classmates. My father has already joined his new workplace, and our family will shift within a few weeks. For this reason I cannot continue my classes here for long. A transfer certificate will help me join the new school in time and continue my studies without a gap. I therefore request you to issue me a transfer certificate at your earliest convenience. I shall remain grateful to you for your kind help in this matter. I hope the new school will admit me without delay once I submit the certificate. Yours obediently, Rahim Class: Ten Roll: 12 Bangla Meaning of the Application for a Transfer Certificate ট্রান্সফার সার্টিফিকেটের আবেদনের বাংলা অর্থ আমি বিনীতভাবে জানাচ্ছি যে আমি আপনার স্কুলের দশম শ্রেণির একজন ছাত্র। আমার বাবার বদলির কারণে আমাদের পরিবার অন্য জেলায় চলে যাবে, তাই আমাকে সেখানেই পড়াশোনা চালিয়ে যেতে হবে। নতুন স্কুল ভর্তির আগে আমার কাছ থেকে ট্রান্সফার সার্টিফিকেট চেয়েছে। আমি স্কুলের সব বেতন পরিশোধ করেছি এবং লাইব্রেরি থেকে নেওয়া বইগুলো ফেরত দিয়েছি। আমি স্কুলের নিয়ম মেনে চলার চেষ্টা করেছি এবং নিয়মিত ক্লাসে উপস্থিত থেকেছি। আমার বাবা ইতিমধ্যে নতুন কর্মস্থলে যোগ দিয়েছেন এবং কয়েক সপ্তাহের মধ্যে আমাদের পরিবার সেখানে চলে যাবে। তাই আমি আর বেশিদিন এখানে ক্লাস করতে পারব না। ট্রান্সফার সার্টিফিকেট পেলে আমি সময়মতো নতুন স্কুলে ভর্তি হতে পারব এবং পড়াশোনায় কোনো ফাঁক পড়বে না। তাই আমি অনুরোধ করছি, আপনি যেন যত তাড়াতাড়ি সম্ভব আমাকে একটি ট্রান্সফার সার্টিফিকেট দেন। সার্টিফিকেটটি জমা দিলে নতুন স্কুল আমাকে দেরি না করে ভর্তি করবে বলে আমি আশা করি। আপনার এই সাহায্যের জন্য আমি কৃতজ্ঞ থাকব। একটি ট্রান্সফার সার্টিফিকেট পুরনো স্কুলের একটি সরকারি কাগজ। এটি প্রমাণ করে যে তুমি সেখানে পড়তে এবং তোমার সব বকেয়া পরিশোধ করা হয়েছে। নতুন স্কুল ভর্তির আগে এটি চায়, তাই আবেদনে নিজের শ্রেণি ও রোল নম্বর সঠিকভাবে লিখতে হবে এবং ভাষা হতে হবে ভদ্র ও পরিষ্কার। Important Word Meanings Learn these words before you write the application. They will help you understand the example and write similar applications in your own words. English Word Bangla Meaning Transfer বদলি Certificate সনদপত্র Respectfully সম্মানের সঙ্গে District জেলা Admission ভর্তি Dues বকেয়া Convenience সুবিধা Grateful কৃতজ্ঞ Issue প্রদান করা Regularly নিয়মিতভাবে Exam Tips Read the question carefully first. The reason for the transfer may be a parent's transfer, a family shift, or a change of residence, so change the reason in the body to match the question. Keep the format in the correct order: date, headmaster, school address, subject, salutation, body, closing, and then your name, class and roll number. Write the body in three short paragraphs: introduce yourself and give the reason, show that your dues are clear, and then make your request politely. Do not memorise the example word by word. Learn the format and the main points, then write the application in your own simple sentences. Check your spelling, the subject line and your class and roll number before you finish, because a small mistake can cost marks. title: Dialogue Bad Effect of Smoking
excerpt: This dialogue is about the bad effects of smoking. It is written for Class 6 to 10, SSC and HSC students. The exam question is usually: "Write a dialogue
plainContent: This dialogue is about the bad effects of smoking. It is written for Class 6 to 10, SSC and HSC students. The exam question is usually: "Write a dialogue between two friends about the bad effects of smoking." Read the dialogue below, then learn the Bangla meaning and the important words at the end. The dialogue uses simple English, so you can learn it easily and rewrite it in your own words in the examination. Dialogue: Bad Effect of Smoking Rafi: My older cousin has started smoking because he thinks it makes him look mature. Joya: Tobacco does not prove maturity. It contains addictive substances and exposes the body to harmful chemicals. Rafi: What damage can smoking cause? Joya: It raises the risk of lung disease, heart problems, stroke, and several cancers. Smoke also harms people nearby, especially children and pregnant women. Rafi: My cousin says he smokes only a few cigarettes a day, so it cannot be dangerous. Joya: Even a small amount is harmful. There is no safe level of smoking, and the damage grows with every year of use. Rafi: Smoking also wastes money, does it not? Joya: Yes. Money spent on cigarettes could support food, books, or savings. A smoker also pays more later for treatment. Rafi: Some people say they can stop whenever they wish. Joya: Dependence makes quitting difficult, but support from a doctor, family, or cessation programme can help. Avoiding triggers and replacing the habit with exercise or another activity is useful. Rafi: What is a trigger? Joya: A trigger is something that makes a person want to smoke — for example, stress, tea with friends, or a break after a meal. If a person knows his triggers, he can prepare for them. Rafi: We should not tease someone who is trying to quit. Joya: Right. Encouragement is more helpful than shame. Young people should learn the facts before advertising or peer pressure influences them. Rafi: Why do young people start smoking at all? Joya: Often because of friends, films, or advertisements that make smoking look attractive. Some start from curiosity and then cannot stop. Rafi: Can schools help to stop this? Joya: Yes. Teachers can explain the dangers, and schools can keep their surroundings free from tobacco. Parents should also talk openly with their children. Rafi: My cousin coughs every morning now. Is that a sign of damage? Joya: It can be. A smoker's cough is a warning. He should see a doctor and stop smoking before the damage becomes serious. Rafi: I will share reliable health information with my cousin and ask whether he wants help. Joya: Good. A calm and honest conversation can do more than a lecture. If he decides to quit, we can support him every step of the way. title: Food Adulteration paragraph for Class 6,7,8, HSC, SSC

plainContent: On this page you will find food adulteration paragraph in 150, 250 and 300 words for Class 6 to 12, SSC and HSC. The short version is best for junior classes, and the longer versions are best for SSC and HSC. A Bangla meaning, important word meanings and exam tips are given at the end. Food Adulteration Paragraph in 150 Words Best for Class 6–7. Food adulteration means mixing inferior, contaminated or harmful substances into food, or using unsafe chemicals to make food look better or last longer. Milk, spices, oil, fruit, fish, sweets and packaged food can all be affected. Greedy sellers do it to earn more money. It is a serious crime against public health. Eating adulterated food may cause stomach pain, vomiting and diarrhoea at once, and it can damage organs after repeated use. Children, old people and sick people face the greatest danger. Adulteration is therefore not a small business offence; it threatens the health of the whole nation. Consumers should buy from reliable shops, check packaging and dates, wash fruit and vegetables, and be careful about unnatural colours or very low prices. We should also report suspicious food to the authorities. Authorities must test food, inspect shops and punish offenders. Honest sellers and informed buyers can help build a safer food market. Food Adulteration Paragraph in 250 Words Best for Class 8–10 and SSC. Food adulteration means mixing inferior, contaminated or harmful substances into food, or using unsafe chemicals to make food look better or last longer. Milk, spices, oil, fruit, fish, sweets and packaged food can all be affected. Greedy sellers do it to earn more money. Formalin, artificial colours and cheap oil are some of the substances dishonest sellers use. It is a serious crime against public health, not a small business trick. Eating adulterated food may cause stomach pain, vomiting and diarrhoea at once, and it can damage organs after repeated use. Children, old people and sick people face the greatest danger. Some chemicals used in food can cause serious illness over time. A mother who feeds her child adulterated milk does not know she is harming the child she loves. Adulteration is therefore not a small business offence; it threatens the health of the whole nation. When people lose trust in food, honest sellers also suffer. Consumers should buy from reliable shops, check packaging and dates, wash fruit and vegetables, and be careful about unnatural colours or very low prices. We should also report suspicious food to the authorities. Authorities must test food, inspect shops and punish offenders. Honest sellers and informed buyers can help build a safer food market and protect every family. Schools and the media should teach people how to spot adulterated food. The government should give strong punishment, because a small fine does not stop a greedy seller. Food Adulteration Paragraph in 300 Words Best for SSC and HSC. title: Drug Addiction Paragraph for Class 6-12, SSC, HSC

plainContent: On this page you will find drug addiction paragraph in 150, 250 and 300 words for Class 6 to 12, SSC and HSC. The short version is best for junior classes, and the longer versions are best for SSC and HSC. A Bangla meaning, important word meanings and exam tips are given at the end. Drug Addiction Paragraph in 150 Words Best for Class 6–7. Drug addiction means a person cannot stop using a harmful drug even when it damages health, study and family life. It often begins with curiosity or pressure from friends. What starts as a small experiment can slowly become a strong dependence. The drug slowly takes control of the person's life. An addicted person may lose interest in study, work and family duties. Drugs damage the body and the mind, waste money and break relationships. Addiction can also lead to accidents and crime, and it brings shame and pain to the whole family. Prevention is better than cure. Education, sports, creative activities and caring families can keep young people away from drugs. Anyone who is addicted should get help from a doctor or a treatment centre. Hiding the problem only makes it worse. We should say no to drugs firmly, but treat affected people with kindness so they can recover. Drug Addiction Paragraph in 250 Words Best for Class 8–10 and SSC. Drug addiction means a person cannot stop using a harmful drug even when it damages health, study and family life. It often begins with curiosity or pressure from friends. What starts as a small experiment can slowly become a strong dependence. The drug slowly takes control of the person's life, and the person needs more and more of it to feel normal. Young people are the most at risk, because they want to try new things and they want to be accepted by their friends. An addicted person may lose interest in study, work and family duties. Drugs damage the body and the mind, waste money and break relationships. The person may steal or borrow money to buy drugs. Addiction can also lead to accidents and crime, and it brings shame and pain to the whole family. Many addicts drop out of school and cannot find a good job later in life. In the end, the addict loses health, money, respect and hope. Prevention is better than cure. Education, sports, creative activities and caring families can keep young people away from drugs. Parents should talk honestly with their children and notice sudden changes in behaviour. Anyone who is addicted should get help from a doctor, a counsellor or a treatment centre. Hiding the problem only makes it worse. We should say no to drugs firmly, but treat affected people with kindness so they can recover. The government should also stop illegal drug trade and make treatment easy to reach. Drug Addiction Paragraph in 300 Words Best for SSC and HSC. We should say no to drugs firmly, but treat affected people with kindness so they can recover. The government should also stop illegal drug trade and make treatment easy to reach. A drug-free life is a healthy and happy life, and every young person deserves that chance. title: A Friend in Need is a Friend Indeed Completing story for all classes
excerpt: This is the completing story of a friend in need, written for Class 6 to 10, SSC and HSC students. The given beginning is: "Two friends were travelling through
plainContent: This is the completing story of a friend in need, written for Class 6 to 10, SSC and HSC students. The given beginning is: "Two friends were travelling through a forest. Suddenly, they heard a bear approaching and one of them climbed a tree." Read the complete story below, then learn the moral, the Bangla meaning and the important words at the end. A Friend in Need is a Friend Indeed (Complete Story) Two friends were travelling through a forest. They had been walking since morning, talking and laughing together. The forest was quiet, and the path was narrow. Suddenly, they heard a bear approaching, and one of them quickly climbed a tree. He did not think of his friend at all. He only thought of his own safety. The other friend was left alone on the ground. He had no time to climb a tree, and he knew he could not run faster than a bear. He remembered that a bear is unlikely to touch a person who appears lifeless, so he held his breath and lay flat on the ground without moving. The bear came close and examined him carefully. It sniffed his face and his ears, and it pushed his body gently with its paw. The man did not move and did not make a sound. At last, the bear decided that the man was dead and moved away into the forest. The man on the ground lay still for a long time even after the bear had gone. His heart was beating fast, and his hands were shaking. At last he stood up slowly and looked around to make sure the forest was safe. He felt angry and sad at the same time, because the friend he trusted had left him alone in danger. When the danger had passed, the man in the tree climbed down. He was smiling, as if nothing serious had happened. He jokingly asked his friend what the bear had whispered in his ear. His companion stood up, dusted his clothes, and replied calmly that the animal had advised him never to trust a person who abandons a friend in danger. The words were calm, but the lesson was serious. The man in the tree felt ashamed. He understood that he had failed the test of friendship. Friendship is not measured by cheerful conversations or shared meals. It is revealed when help is inconvenient and fear is real. A dependable friend offers support instead of searching for personal safety first. The two friends continued their journey, but the friendship was never the same again. The man who had been left alone learned to choose his friends more carefully, and the other learned that a true friend stands beside us during difficulty. Moral A true friend stands beside us during difficulty. A friend in need is a friend indeed. Bangla Meaning of the Story গল্পটির বাংলা অর্থ দুই বন্ধু বনের মধ্যে দিয়ে যাচ্ছিল। হঠাৎ তারা একটি ভালুক আসছে শুনতে পেল। একজন দ্রুত গাছে উঠে গেল, আর অন্যজন মাটিতে পড়ে রইল। সে জানত, ভালুক মৃত মনে করা মানুষকে স্পর্শ করে না। তাই সে নিঃশ্বাস বন্ধ করে নিশ্চল হয়ে শুয়ে রইল। ভালুক কাছে এসে তাকে ভালোভাবে পরীক্ষা করল, তার মুখ ও কান শুঁকল। শেষে তাকে মৃত মনে করে চলে গেল। বিপদ কেটে গেলে গাছের বন্ধুটি নেমে এসে মজা করে জিজ্ঞেস করল, ভালুক তার কানে কী বলেছে। বন্ধুটি শান্তভাবে উত্তর দিল, ভালুক তাকে পরামর্শ দিয়েছে বিপদে বন্ধুকে ফেলে পালিয়ে যাওয়া মানুষকে কখনো বিশ্বাস না করতে। বন্ধুত্বের আসল পরীক্ষা হয় বিপদের সময়েই। ভালুক চলে যাওয়ার পরও লোকটি অনেকক্ষণ নিশ্চল হয়ে শুয়ে রইল। তার বুক ধড়ফড় করছিল এবং হাত কাঁপছিল। অবশেষে সে ধীরে ধীরে উঠে দাঁড়াল এবং চারদিকে তাকিয়ে দেখল বন নিরাপদ কি না। একই সঙ্গে তার রাগ ও দুঃখ হচ্ছিল, কারণ যাকে সে বিশ্বাস করত সেই বন্ধুই তাকে বিপদে একা ফেলে গিয়েছিল। Important Word Meanings English Word Bangla Meaning Approaching কাছে আসছে এমন Abandon পরিত্যাগ করা, ফেলে যাওয়া Lifeless প্রাণহীন Examine পরীক্ষা করা Whisper ফিসফিস করে বলা Companion সঙ্গী Ashamed লজ্জিত Dependable নির্ভরযোগ্য Revealed প্রকাশ পাওয়া Difficulty বিপদ, কষ্ট Exam Tips Begin the story with the given beginning exactly as it is written in the question, then continue it in your own words. Keep the events in order: the bear appears, one friend climbs the tree, the other pretends to be dead, the bear leaves, and the friend gives his reply. Write in the past tense, because the story happened in the past. Do not change the main idea of the story. The friend on the ground must survive by his own presence of mind, and the moral must come from his reply. End the story with the moral in a separate short paragraph, as shown above. Write the friend's reply as direct speech. The reply carries the moral, so it should be clear and complete. title: Computer Paragraph for Class 6,7,8, SSC and HSC
excerpt: On this page you will find computer paragraph in 150, 250 and 300 words for Class 6 to 12, SSC and HSC. The short version is best for junior classes, and the
plainContent: On this page you will find computer paragraph in 150, 250 and 300 words for Class 6 to 12, SSC and HSC. The short version is best for junior classes, and the longer versions are best for SSC and HSC. A Bangla meaning, important word meanings and exam tips are given at the end. Computer Paragraph in 150 Words Best for Class 6–7. A computer is an electronic machine that works with information. It can store, calculate, sort and show data very quickly and accurately. It follows instructions given by people through programs. Today computers are used in offices, hospitals, banks, shops, schools and homes all over the world. For students, a computer is a great helper. A learner can type an assignment, organise information, calculate expenses, draw a chart or attend an online class. Students can also read digital books and practise languages with the same device. Job seekers can prepare applications and learn professional skills on a computer. But a computer must be used wisely. Users should keep strong passwords, download files carefully and protect their privacy. Children should ask an adult before downloading a new game or app. Too much screen time can harm health and study. Used with balance, a computer saves time, encourages creativity and opens the door to knowledge. Computer Paragraph in 250 Words Best for Class 8–10 and SSC. A computer is an electronic machine that works with information. It can store, calculate, sort and show data very quickly and accurately. It follows instructions given by people through programs. Today computers are used in offices, hospitals, banks, shops, schools and homes all over the world, and almost every modern workplace depends on them. A computer never gets tired, and it can repeat the same work thousands of times without a mistake. For students, a computer is a great helper. A learner can type an assignment, organise information, calculate expenses, draw a chart or attend an online class. Students can also read digital books, visit digital libraries and practise languages with the same device. Job seekers can prepare applications and learn professional skills on a computer. In this way, knowing how to use a computer opens the door to knowledge and to better work. Teachers use computers to prepare lessons, keep records and share study materials with students. But a computer must be used wisely, and users must learn online safety as well as technical skills. Users should keep strong passwords, download files carefully and protect their privacy. Children should ask an adult before downloading a new game or app. Too much screen time can harm health, sleep and study habits. If we keep a balance, a computer saves time, encourages creativity and connects people with useful opportunities. Schools should teach computer skills to every student, because a person who understands the basics can adapt to new software and work with more confidence. Computer Paragraph in 300 Words Best for SSC and HSC. A computer is an electronic machine that works with information. It can store, calculate, sort and show data very quickly and accurately. It follows instructions given by people through programs. Today computers are used in offices, hospitals, banks, shops, schools and homes all over the world, and almost every modern workplace depends on them. A computer never gets tired, and it can repeat the same work thousands of times without a mistake. It has changed the way people write letters, keep accounts, design buildings and share news. For students, a computer is a great helper. A learner can type an assignment, organise information, calculate expenses, draw a chart or attend an online class. Students can also read digital books, visit digital libraries and practise languages with the same device. Job seekers can prepare applications and learn professional skills on a computer. In this way, knowing how to use a computer opens the door to knowledge and to better work. Teachers use computers to prepare lessons, keep records and share study materials with students. Offices use computers to store records, send messages and prepare reports in a few minutes. But a computer must be used wisely, and users must learn online safety as well as technical skills. Users should keep strong passwords, download files carefully and protect their privacy. Children should ask an adult before downloading a new game or app. Too much screen time can harm health, sleep and study habits. If we keep a balance, a computer saves time, encourages creativity and connects people with useful opportunities. Schools should teach computer skills to every student, because a person who understands the basics can adapt to new software and work with more confidence. Games and videos are enjoyable, but they should not take the place of study, play and family time. Bangla Meaning of Computer Paragraph কম্পিউটার অনুচ্ছেদের বাংলা অর্থ কম্পিউটার একটি ইলেকট্রনিক যন্ত্র, যা তথ্য নিয়ে কাজ করে। এটি দ্রুত ও নির্ভুলভাবে হিসাব করতে পারে, তথ্য সংরক্ষণ করতে পারে এবং ছবি ও লেখা দেখাতে পারে। আজ অফিস, হাসপাতাল, ব্যাংক, দোকান ও স্কুল—সব জায়গায় কম্পিউটার ব্যবহৃত হয়। ছাত্রছাত্রীদের জন্য কম্পিউটার বড় সহায়ক। এতে অ্যাসাইনমেন্ট টাইপ করা যায়, অনলাইন ক্লাস করা যায় এবং বই পড়া যায়। তবে কম্পিউটার বুদ্ধিমত্তার সঙ্গে ব্যবহার করা উচিত। শক্ত পাসওয়ার্ড রাখা, সাবধানে ডাউনলোড করা এবং ব্যক্তিগত তথ্য গোপন রাখা জরুরি। অতিরিক্ত স্ক্রিন সময় স্বাস্থ্য ও পড়াশোনার ক্ষতি করে। ভারসাম্য রেখে ব্যবহার করলে কম্পিউটার সময় বাঁচায়, সৃজনশীলতা বাড়ায় এবং জ্ঞানের দরজা খুলে দেয়। Important Word Meanings English Word Bangla Meaning Electronic ইলেকট্রনিক Information তথ্য Accurately নির্ভুলভাবে Assignment অ্যাসাইনমেন্ট Organise গোছানো Privacy গোপনীয়তা Creativity সৃজনশীলতা Knowledge জ্ঞান Balance ভারসাম্য Professional পেশাগত Exam Tips Choose the version that matches your class: 150 words for Class 6–7, 250 words for Class 8–10 and SSC, 300 words for SSC and HSC. Do not memorise the whole paragraph word by word. Learn the main points — what a computer does, its uses for students, and safe use — and write them in your own sentences. Write about both sides: the benefits of computers and the need for balance and safety. Use the Bangla meaning to understand difficult words before you memorise the English version. Revise the paragraph once the night before the exam instead of reading it for the first time in the hall. title: Application for Leave of Absence: Class 6 to 12 Students
excerpt: On this page you will find an application for leave of absence for Class 6 to 12 students. It shows the correct format and gives a complete example for absence
plainContent: On this page you will find an application for leave of absence for Class 6 to 12 students. It shows the correct format and gives a complete example for absence because of illness, which you can change to fit your own reason. A Bangla meaning, important word meanings and exam tips are given at the end. Format of an Application for Leave of Absence A leave application follows the usual format of a formal application to the headteacher or principal. Each part has a fixed place, so learn the order first and then practise writing the full application. The main parts are given below. Date Name and designation of the headteacher Name of the school Subject of the application Salutation, such as "Sir/Madam" Body of the application Closing, such as "Yours obediently" Name, class, roll number and date of the student Leave of absence means permission to stay away from school for a few days. In the body you must clearly write the dates of your absence, the reason for it, and what you will do about the lessons you miss. A short and honest application is always better than a long one. Application for Leave of Absence (Example) To The Headteacher [School Name] Subject: Application for leave of absence Sir/Madam, I could not attend school from [date] to [date] because I was suffering from fever. A doctor advised me to take complete rest for a few days, and my guardian informed the school as soon as my illness became clear. I am now well enough to return to my classes. During my illness I stayed at home and took the medicine the doctor prescribed. My parents looked after me carefully, and I followed the doctor's advice about food and rest. That is why I have recovered quickly and I am ready to join my classes again. Please excuse my absence for the stated period. I have collected the class notes from a classmate and I will complete the lessons, homework and class tests that I missed. I have also asked my teachers about the lessons I missed. A medical certificate is enclosed with this application, as the school may wish to see it. I shall be grateful if you kindly grant me leave for the stated period. I promise to attend my classes regularly from now on and to work hard to make up for the lessons I have missed. Yours obediently, Rahim Class: Eight | Roll: 15 Date: [date] Bangla Meaning of the Application for Leave of Absence ছুটির আবেদনের বাংলা অর্থ জ্বরে আক্রান্ত হওয়ার কারণে আমি [তারিখ] থেকে [তারিখ] পর্যন্ত স্কুলে যেতে পারিনি। ডাক্তার আমাকে কয়েকদিন সম্পূর্ণ বিশ্রাম নিতে বলেছিলেন এবং আমার অসুস্থতার কথা জানার সঙ্গে সঙ্গেই আমার অভিভাবক স্কুলকে জানিয়েছিলেন। এখন আমি সুস্থ হয়ে ক্লাসে ফিরতে পারব। অসুস্থতার সময় আমি বাড়িতে ছিলাম এবং ডাক্তারের দেওয়া ওষুধ খেয়েছি। আমার বাবা-মা যত্ন করে আমার দেখাশোনা করেছেন এবং আমি খাওয়া ও বিশ্রাম সম্পর্কে ডাক্তারের পরামর্শ মেনে চলেছি। তাই আমি তাড়াতাড়ি সুস্থ হয়ে উঠেছি এবং আবার ক্লাসে যোগ দিতে প্রস্তুত। আমি অনুরোধ করছি, উল্লিখিত সময়ের জন্য আমার অনুপস্থিতি যেন ক্ষমা করা হয়। আমি সহপাঠীর কাছ থেকে ক্লাসের নোট সংগ্রহ করেছি এবং ছুটে যাওয়া পাঠ, বাড়ির কাজ ও ক্লাস পরীক্ষাগুলো শেষ করব। শিক্ষকদের কাছেও আমি ছুটে যাওয়া পাঠ সম্পর্কে জেনে নিয়েছি। স্কুল চাইলে দেখতে পারে, তাই এই আবেদনের সঙ্গে একটি চিকিৎসা সনদ দেওয়া হয়েছে। আপনি যদি দয়া করে উল্লিখিত সময়ের জন্য আমাকে ছুটি দেন, আমি কৃতজ্ঞ থাকব। আমি এখন থেকে নিয়মিত ক্লাসে উপস্থিত থাকব এবং ছুটে যাওয়া পাঠগুলো পূরণ করার জন্য কঠোর পরিশ্রম করব বলে প্রতিজ্ঞা করছি। Important Word Meanings Learn these words before you write the application. They will help you understand the example and write similar applications in your own words. English Word Bangla Meaning Absence অনুপস্থিতি Suffering ভোগা Advise পরামর্শ দেওয়া Guardian অভিভাবক Recover সুস্থ হওয়া Excuse ক্ষমা করা Enclosed সংযুক্ত Medical চিকিৎসা সংক্রান্ত Grant মঞ্জুর করা Regularly নিয়মিতভাবে Exam Tips Read the question carefully first. The reason for leave may be illness, a family event, or an urgent journey, so change the reason and the dates in the body to match the question. Always write the dates of your absence clearly. If the question gives the dates, use those dates; if it does not, write the dates in the same style as the example. Keep the format in the correct order: date, headteacher, school name, subject, salutation, body, closing, and then your name, class, roll number and date. Write the body in three or four short paragraphs: give the reason, explain what happened, say how you will cover the missed lessons, and then make your request politely. Do not memorise the example word by word. Learn the format and the main points, then write the application in your own simple sentences and check your spelling before you finish.
