title: Application for Testimonial For Class 6, 7, 8, SSC and HSC
excerpt: On this page you will find an application for a testimonial for Class 6, 7, 8, SSC and HSC students. It explains what a testimonial is, shows the correct
plainContent: On this page you will find an application for a testimonial for Class 6, 7, 8, SSC and HSC students. It explains what a testimonial is, shows the correct format, and gives a complete example that you can follow in your examination. A Bangla meaning, important word meanings and exam tips are given at the end. Format of an Application for a Testimonial A testimonial application follows the usual format of a formal application to the headmaster or principal. Each part has a fixed place, so learn the order first and then practise writing the full application. The main parts are given below. Date Name and designation of the headmaster or principal Name and address of the school Subject of the application Salutation, such as "Sir" Body of the application Closing, such as "Yours obediently" Name, class and roll number of the student A testimonial is an official paper from your school or college. It describes your conduct, your academic record and the period of your study there. Students usually need it after SSC or HSC, when they apply for college admission or higher studies, so write the application in clear and polite language. Application for a Testimonial (Example) 18 July 2025 The Headmaster Pabna Zilla School Pabna Subject: Request for a testimonial Sir, I respectfully state that I was a student of your school in Class Ten during the academic year 2024–2025. I completed the Secondary School Certificate examination from this institution, and I have now been admitted to a college. The college authorities have asked me to submit a testimonial describing my conduct and academic record. I maintained regular attendance, followed the rules of the school, and took part in academic and co-curricular activities. My teachers guided me with care, and I always tried to behave politely with my classmates. I also took part in the annual sports and cultural programmes of the school whenever I got the chance. During my time at school I learned not only from my lessons but also from my teachers and friends. The school taught me discipline, honesty and respect for others. I will always remember these lessons and try to follow them in my college life. I therefore request you to issue me a testimonial at your earliest convenience. I shall remain grateful to you for your kind help. I hope the testimonial will help me complete my college admission without delay. Yours obediently, Rahim Class: Ten Roll: 12 Bangla Meaning of the Application for a Testimonial প্রশংসাপত্রের আবেদনের বাংলা অর্থ আমি বিনীতভাবে জানাচ্ছি যে আমি ২০২৪–২০২৫ শিক্ষাবর্ষে আপনার স্কুলের দশম শ্রেণির ছাত্র ছিলাম। আমি এই প্রতিষ্ঠান থেকে মাধ্যমিক স্কুল সার্টিফিকেট পরীক্ষা সম্পন্ন করেছি এবং এখন একটি কলেজে ভর্তি হয়েছি। কলেজ কর্তৃপক্ষ আমার আচরণ ও শিক্ষাগত ফলাফল সম্পর্কে একটি প্রশংসাপত্র জমা দিতে বলেছে। আমি নিয়মিত উপস্থিত থেকেছি, স্কুলের নিয়ম মেনে চলেছি এবং পড়াশোনা ও সহপাঠক্রমিক কার্যক্রমে অংশ নিয়েছি। শিক্ষকরা যত্ন করে আমাকে পথ দেখিয়েছেন এবং আমি সবসময় সহপাঠীদের সঙ্গে ভদ্রভাবে আচরণ করার চেষ্টা করেছি। সুযোগ পেলেই আমি স্কুলের বার্ষিক ক্রীড়া ও সাংস্কৃতিক অনুষ্ঠানেও অংশ নিয়েছি। স্কুলে থাকার সময় আমি শুধু পাঠ থেকেই নয়, শিক্ষক ও বন্ধুদের কাছ থেকেও অনেক কিছু শিখেছি। স্কুল আমাকে শৃঙ্খলা, সততা ও অন্যদের প্রতি সম্মান শিখিয়েছে। আমি এই শিক্ষাগুলো সবসময় মনে রাখব এবং কলেজ জীবনেও সেগুলো মেনে চলার চেষ্টা করব। তাই আমি অনুরোধ করছি, আপনি যেন যত তাড়াতাড়ি সম্ভব আমাকে একটি প্রশংসাপত্র দেন। আপনার এই সাহায্যের জন্য আমি কৃতজ্ঞ থাকব। প্রশংসাপত্রটি পেলে আমার কলেজে ভর্তি দেরি না করে সম্পন্ন হবে বলে আমি আশা করি। Important Word Meanings Learn these words before you write the application. They will help you understand the example and write similar applications in your own words. English Word Bangla Meaning Testimonial প্রশংসাপত্র Respectfully সম্মানের সঙ্গে Academic শিক্ষাগত Conduct আচরণ Institution প্রতিষ্ঠান Authorities কর্তৃপক্ষ Co-curricular সহপাঠক্রমিক Convenience সুবিধা Grateful কৃতজ্ঞ Issue প্রদান করা Exam Tips Read the question carefully first. The student in the question may have passed SSC or HSC, so change the class, the examination and the academic year in the body to match the question. Keep the format in the correct order: date, headmaster or principal, school address, subject, salutation, body, closing, and then your name, class and roll number. Write the body in three or four short paragraphs: introduce yourself and give the reason, describe your attendance and conduct, and then make your request politely. Do not confuse a testimonial with a transfer certificate. A testimonial describes your conduct and academic record, while a transfer certificate proves that you studied at the school and cleared your dues. Do not memorise the example word by word. Learn the format and the main points, then write the application in your own simple sentences and check your spelling before you finish. title: Traffic Jam Paragraph for class 6,7,8, SSC
excerpt: On this page you will find traffic jam paragraph in 150, 250 and 300 words for Class 6 to 12, SSC and HSC. The short version is best for junior classes, and
plainContent: On this page you will find traffic jam paragraph in 150, 250 and 300 words for Class 6 to 12, SSC and HSC. The short version is best for junior classes, and the longer versions are best for SSC and HSC. A Bangla meaning, important word meanings and exam tips are given at the end. Traffic Jam Paragraph in 150 Words Best for Class 6–7. A traffic jam is a long queue of vehicles moving slowly or not at all. It is common in crowded cities where the number of cars, buses, trucks, rickshaws and motorcycles has grown faster than the roads. Dhaka is one of the cities where traffic jams are a daily problem. Narrow streets, road repairs, illegal parking and careless driving make it worse. A jam wastes valuable time and fuel. Students may miss classes, workers arrive late, and patients can face dangerous delays. Exhaust fumes increase air pollution, while constant horns create stress and noise. Goods reach shops more slowly, which raises business costs. Better public transport can reduce the number of private vehicles. Authorities should improve signals, create safe footpaths and parking areas, and enforce traffic rules. Traffic police also need good training and equipment. Citizens should plan their journeys and follow directions patiently. Cooperation can make city travel safer and faster. Traffic Jam Paragraph in 250 Words Best for Class 8–10 and SSC. A traffic jam is a long queue of vehicles moving slowly or not at all. It is common in crowded cities where the number of cars, buses, trucks, rickshaws and motorcycles has grown faster than the roads. Dhaka is one of the cities where traffic jams are a daily problem. Every morning and evening, the main roads of Dhaka fill with slow-moving traffic. Narrow streets, road repairs, illegal parking, roadside markets, poor signals and careless driving make congestion worse. A jam wastes valuable time and fuel. Students may miss classes, workers arrive late, and patients can face dangerous delays. Exhaust fumes increase air pollution, while constant horns create stress and noise. Goods reach shops more slowly, which raises business costs. People waiting in a jam feel tired, angry and helpless, and this harms their health and mood. A single jam can delay thousands of people and waste hours that could be used for study or work. Better public transport can reduce the number of private vehicles. Authorities should improve signals, create safe footpaths and parking areas, remove illegal obstructions and enforce lane and stopping rules. Traffic police also need good training and equipment. Citizens should plan their journeys, avoid blocking intersections and follow directions patiently. Schools should also teach children road rules so that the next generation drives and walks safely. Long-term city planning that places homes, workplaces and services near reliable transport is essential. Cooperation between planners, drivers, pedestrians and businesses can make city travel safer and faster. Traffic Jam Paragraph in 300 Words Best for SSC and HSC. A traffic jam is a long queue of vehicles moving slowly or not at all. It is common in crowded cities where the number of cars, buses, trucks, rickshaws and motorcycles has grown faster than the roads. Dhaka is one of the cities where traffic jams are a daily problem. Every morning and evening, the main roads of Dhaka fill with slow-moving traffic. When too many vehicles try to use a narrow road at the same time, the result is a jam. Narrow streets, road repairs, illegal parking, roadside markets, poor signals and careless driving make congestion worse. A jam wastes valuable time and fuel. Students may miss classes, workers arrive late, and patients can face dangerous delays. Exhaust fumes increase air pollution, while constant horns create stress and noise. Goods reach shops more slowly, which raises business costs. People waiting in a jam feel tired, angry and helpless, and this harms their health and mood. Ambulances stuck in traffic cannot reach hospitals in time, and that can cost a life. A single jam can delay thousands of people and waste hours that could be used for study or work. Better public transport can reduce the number of private vehicles. Authorities should improve signals, create safe footpaths and parking areas, remove illegal obstructions and enforce lane and stopping rules. Traffic police also need good training and equipment. Citizens should plan their journeys, avoid blocking intersections and follow directions patiently. Schools should also teach children road rules so that the next generation drives and walks safely. Long-term city planning that places homes, workplaces and services near reliable transport is essential. Cooperation between planners, drivers, pedestrians and businesses can make city travel safer and faster. A city that moves well is a city that works well, and every citizen has a part to play in it. Bangla Meaning of Traffic Jam Paragraph যানজট অনুচ্ছেদের বাংলা অর্থ যানজট মানে যানবাহনের দীর্ঘ সারি ধীরে চলা বা একেবারে থেমে যাওয়া। জনবহুল শহরে গাড়ি, বাস, ট্রাক, রিকশা ও মোটরসাইকেলের সংখ্যা রাস্তার চেয়ে দ্রুত বেড়েছে। ঢাকায় যানজট প্রতিদিনের সমস্যা। যানজট মূল্যবান সময় ও জ্বালানি নষ্ট করে। ছাত্ররা ক্লাস মিস করে, কর্মীরা দেরিতে পৌঁছায়, আর রোগীরা বিপজ্জনক দেরির মুখে পড়ে। গাড়ির ধোঁয়া বায়ুদূষণ বাড়ায়। ভালো গণপরিবহন ব্যক্তিগত গাড়ির সংখ্যা কমাতে পারে। কর্তৃপক্ষের উচিত সংকেত উন্নত করা, নিরাপদ ফুটপাত ও পার্কিংয়ের ব্যবস্থা করা এবং ট্রাফিক নিয়ম কার্যকর করা। নাগরিকদেরও ধৈর্য ধরে নিয়ম মানা উচিত। সবার সহযোগিতায় শহরের যাতায়াত নিরাপদ ও দ্রুত হতে পারে। Important Word Meanings English Word Bangla Meaning Congestion যানজট Queue সারি Exhaust ধোঁয়া Obstruction প্রতিবন্ধকতা Intersection মোড় Pedestrian পথচারী Enforce কার্যকর করা Patiently ধৈর্যের সঙ্গে Essential অপরিহার্য Cooperation সহযোগিতা Exam Tips Choose the version that matches your class: 150 words for Class 6–7, 250 words for Class 8–10 and SSC, 300 words for SSC and HSC. Do not memorise the whole paragraph word by word. Learn the main points — causes of jams, their effects, and solutions — and write them in your own sentences. Give both causes and solutions. A paragraph with only problems and no solution looks incomplete. Use the Bangla meaning to understand difficult words before you memorise the English version. Revise the paragraph once the night before the exam instead of reading it for the first time in the hall. title: A Thirsty Crow completing story For Class 6,7,8, SSC and HSC
excerpt: This is the completing story of a thirsty crow, written for Class 6 to 10, SSC and HSC students. The given beginning is: "Once, on a hot summer day, a crow was
plainContent: This is the completing story of a thirsty crow, written for Class 6 to 10, SSC and HSC students. The given beginning is: "Once, on a hot summer day, a crow was very thirsty. It flew here and there in search of water but found none." Read the complete story below, then learn the moral, the Bangla meaning and the important words at the end. The story teaches us that intelligence and patience can solve a problem that strength cannot. A Thirsty Crow (Complete Story) Once, on a hot summer day, a crow was very thirsty. It flew here and there in search of water, but it found none. The sun was hot, the fields were dry, and every pond the crow knew had dried up. At last, tired and hopeless, it sat on the branch of a tree and looked around once more. Then it saw a jar standing in a corner of a yard. The crow flew down quickly and looked inside. A little water lay at the bottom of the jar, but the jar was tall and narrow. The crow pushed its beak inside, but it could not reach the water. It tried to tip the jar over, yet the vessel was too heavy. It pushed the jar with its wings and its feet, but the jar did not move. The crow felt very sad. It had found water at last, but the water was useless. It looked around the yard for another source and found none. For a moment, it thought of flying away and giving up. Then it noticed some small pebbles lying near the jar. A new idea came into its mind. It picked up a pebble with its beak and dropped it into the jar. Then it brought another pebble, and another. The work was slow, and the crow was tired, but it did not stop. The water rose little by little, and the crow worked with more hope. The other birds watched from the trees and wondered what the crow was doing. Some of them laughed at the slow work. But the crow paid no attention to them. It knew that dropping pebbles was the only way to bring the water within reach. Each pebble made a small sound as it fell, and each sound gave the crow a little more hope. After a long time, the water reached the rim of the jar. At last the crow drank the cool water to its heart's content. Its wings felt light again, and it flew away happily, calling out to the other birds as it went. The solution was not quick, but patient observation had turned a difficult problem into a manageable task. When the first plan fails, a person can examine the materials at hand, think step by step, and continue working rather than complain. Moral Intelligence, patience, and perseverance can overcome obstacles. Bangla Meaning of the Story গল্পটির বাংলা অর্থ এক গ্রীষ্মের গরম দিনে একটি কাকের খুব পিপাসা পেল। সে পানির খোঁজে এদিক-ওদিক উড়ল, কিন্তু কোথাও পানি পেল না। রোদ ছিল প্রচণ্ড, মাঠ ছিল শুকনো, আর কাকের চেনা পুকুরগুলোও শুকিয়ে গিয়েছিল। অবশেষে সে একটি উঠানের কোণে একটি কলসি দেখতে পেল। কলসির তলায় অল্প পানি ছিল, কিন্তু কলসিটি ছিল উঁচু ও সরু। কাক তার ঠোঁট ঢুকিয়েও পানির নাগাল পেল না। কলসিটি উল্টানোর চেষ্টা করল, কিন্তু তা খুব ভারী ছিল। তখন সে কাছাকাছি ছোট ছোট নুড়ি পাথর দেখতে পেল। একটি একটি করে পাথর কলসিতে ফেলতে লাগল। ধীরে ধীরে পানি উপরে উঠে এলো। শেষে কাক তৃপ্তি করে পানি পান করল এবং খুশি মনে উড়ে গেল। অন্য পাখিরা গাছ থেকে দেখে ভাবছিল কাক কী করছে। কেউ কেউ তার ধীর কাজ দেখে হাসছিল, কিন্তু কাক সেদিকে মনোযোগ দেয়নি। সে জানত, পাথর ফেলাই পানিকে নাগালের মধ্যে আনার একমাত্র উপায়। প্রতিটি পাথর পড়ার শব্দ তাকে আরও আশা দিচ্ছিল। ধীরে ধীরে চেষ্টা করলে কঠিন কাজও সহজ হয় — এই গল্পের শিক্ষা এটাই। Important Word Meanings English Word Bangla Meaning Thirsty তৃষ্ণার্ত Vessel পাত্র Narrow সরু Pebble নুড়ি পাথর Hopeless হতাশ Observation পর্যবেক্ষণ Patient ধৈর্যশীল Perseverance অধ্যবসায় Obstacle বাধা Manageable সামলানো যায় এমন Exam Tips Begin the story with the given beginning exactly as it is written in the question, then continue it in your own words. Keep the events in order: the crow's thirst, the jar, the failed attempts, the pebbles, and the success at the end. Write in the past tense, because the story happened in the past. Do not change the main idea of the story. The crow must solve the problem with its intelligence and patience. End the story with the moral in a separate short paragraph, as shown above. Keep the story short and clear. Do not add new characters or new problems that are not in the original story. title: HSC GPA Calculator
plainContent: Calculate your HSC GPA online using your subject marks or letter grades. This free HSC GPA Calculator supports Science, Business Studies, and Humanities students in Bangladesh and automatically applies the applicable 4th-subject bonus . Enter your marks or grades below to calculate your estimated GPA, total grade points, and equivalent percentage. Group Science Business Studies Humanities Main subjects Enter a letter grade OR marks. Marks fields take the total out of 200 (out of 100 for ICT). Optional subject (4th subject bonus) Optional subject Calculate GPA Reset Note: This calculator provides an estimate based on the Bangladesh HSC grading system. Your official GPA is the result shown on the marksheet issued by the relevant education board. HSC GPA Calculator Bangladesh 2026 The HSC GPA Calculator helps students estimate their Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) Grade Point Average from their subject results. You can enter either your letter grades or your marks . The calculator converts your marks into the corresponding grade points and calculates your overall GPA. It supports the three main HSC groups: Science Business Studies Humanities The calculator also supports the 4th or optional subject , allowing the applicable bonus to be included automatically. If you already have your marks or grades, enter them above to get your estimated HSC GPA. How to Calculate HSC GPA Bangladesh's HSC grading system uses a 5.00-point scale . Each subject result is converted into a letter grade and corresponding grade point. For example: 80–100 marks = A+ = 5.00 70–79 marks = A = 4.00 60–69 marks = A− = 3.50 50–59 marks = B = 3.00 40–49 marks = C = 2.00 33–39 marks = D = 1.00 0–32 marks = F = 0.00 The official Education Board grading table uses this marks-to-grade-point scale. For the main subjects, the grade points are used to determine the student's GPA. If an optional or 4th subject is included, the applicable bonus is added according to the grading rules. Simple example Suppose a student receives these grade points: Subject Grade Grade Point Bangla A+ 5.00 English A 4.00 ICT A+ 5.00 Physics A+ 5.00 Chemistry A 4.00 Biology A+ 5.00 The grade points from the main subjects are used to calculate the student's GPA. If the student also has an optional subject, the 4th-subject rule is applied before the final GPA is determined. HSC Grading System in Bangladesh The HSC grading system uses a 5.00 GPA scale. The following table shows the standard marks-to-grade conversion used by Bangladesh's Education Boards. Marks Letter Grade Grade Point 80–100 A+ 5.00 70–79 A 4.00 60–69 A− 3.50 50–59 B 3.00 40–49 C 2.00 33–39 D 1.00 0–32 F 0.00 What do the grades mean? A+ (5.00) The highest grade point on the HSC grading scale. A (4.00) A strong result with a grade point of 4.00. A− (3.50) A grade point of 3.50. B (3.00) A grade point of 3.00. C (2.00) A grade point of 2.00. D (1.00) The minimum passing grade. F (0.00) A failing grade in the subject. HSC 4th Subject Bonus: How Does It Work? The 4th subject, also called the optional subject , is treated differently from the main subjects. When the grade point earned in the optional subject is above 2.00 , the amount above 2.00 is treated as the bonus. For example: Optional subject grade point = 5.00 Then: 5.00 − 2.00 = 3.00 bonus points Similarly: Optional subject grade point = 4.00 4.00 − 2.00 = 2.00 bonus points And: Optional subject grade point = 3.50 3.50 − 2.00 = 1.50 bonus points The bonus is then incorporated into the overall GPA calculation according to the applicable HSC rules. Our calculator applies the 4th-subject calculation automatically, so you do not need to calculate the bonus manually. If you have an optional subject, enter it separately in the 4th Subject field so that the applicable bonus can be included.
